articles.title: Learning by moving: Physical motion accelerates category learning
articles.authors: Luke Rosedahl, Yuka Sasaki, Takeo Watanabe
articles.abstract: Categorization is crucial for survival, helping animals forage, navigate, and avoid predators—all tasks involving movement. Yet, dominant theories of category learning treat it as a purely cognitive or perceptual process. Here, we challenge this view by demonstrating that physical movement can enhance category learning—but selectively. Using immersive virtual reality, we found that performing large actions, such as swinging a lightsaber, substantially improved learning of categories requiring integration of multiple cues (e.g., distinguishing aggressive from noncancerous lesions), while having minimal impact on categories involving independent evaluation of features (e.g., sorting by color and shape). This selective enhancement reveals a previously unrecognized motor contribution to categorization and may explain why prior studies missed it, opening avenues for optimizing training in critical categorization tasks.

articles_hidden.title: Loss of KAT5-dependent H2A.Z acetylation provokes chromosomal instability in recurrent pregnancy loss
articles_hidden.authors: Shilei Bi, Yongjie Chen, Lizi Zhang, Jiahui Zhang, Yijing Wang, Baoying Huang, Shanze Li, Lijun Huang, Yifan Wang, Huarong Wang, Ranran Meng, Zhaowei Tu, Lili Du, Haibin Wang, Zhijian Wang, Dunjin Chen, Shuang Zhang, Fengchao Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Placenta defects are one of the major causes of miscarriages, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that trophoblast-specific depletion of the acetyltransferase Kat5 , or introduction of acetylation-defective mutants Kat5-Q377E G380E and Kat5-Y47A , induces severe chromosomal instability (CIN) during trophoblast cells division, leading to embryonic lethality. Moreover, mutation of a key lysine acetyltransferase 5 (KAT5) substrate, H2A.Z, via the introduction of H2az1-K5R K8R K12R K14R (which prevents H2A.Z acetylation), phenocopies the effects of KAT5 loss. Integrated RNA sequencing and CUT&Tag in mouse trophoblast stem cells reveal that KAT5, through H2A.Z acetylation, regulates transcription of key mitotic genes ( Aurka , Aurkb , and Cenpa ). We extend our finding to human trophoblast stem cells, demonstrating a conserved role for KAT5 in preventing CIN. Clinical analysis of placental villi from recurrent pregnancy loss patients with copy number variations revealed reduced expression of KAT5 and acetylated H2A.Z. This study demonstrates that the conserved KAT5–H2A.Z acetylation pathway safeguards chromosomal stability in trophoblast cells, supporting placenta development and successful pregnancy.

articles_hidden.title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
articles_hidden.authors: Zhizhi Wu, Fan Chen, Jiaheng Liang, Yufei Zhang, Qiyao Huang, Chi Zhang, Peng Li, Shanghang Li, Haihua Shu, Xin Cheng, Hwa-Yaw Tam, Yunfei Chai, Zijian Zheng
articles_hidden.abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na + ) and potassium (K + ), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na + and K + ions in real time directly in the bloodstream. MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS’s superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

articles_hidden.title: Gradient-interlayer–based flexible pressure sensors for high-performance robotic perception
articles_hidden.authors: Mingyuan Sun, Gang Ma, Shuai Dong, Erlong Wang, Shi-Yang Tang, Xuanhan Chen, Yipu Guo, Xiaoqin Sun, Xiangpeng Li, Weihua Li, Shiwu Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Tactile perception systems based on flexible pressure sensors are indispensable for humanoid robots to perform dexterous manipulation, compliant interaction, and operation in visually challenging environments. Although strategies relying on surface or spatial microstructure engineering have improved sensor performance, the long-standing trade-off among sensitivity, sensing range, and linearity continues to hinder their practical deployment. Inspired by the gradient distribution of mechanoreceptors in human fingertip skin, we report a gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic pressure sensor (GriFIPS) in which a single direct-ink-written elastomeric mesh-like interlayer, with a centrifugal increase in aperture size, is placed between the soft electrode and an ionic hydrogel layer. Operating upstream of the functional layer, the mesh enables progressive, stage-wise contact under increasing load and decouples macroscopic contact-area evolution from the microscopic interfacial response. The sensor simultaneously achieves a sensitivity of 175.9 kPa −1 , a linear sensing range up to 360 kPa with a coefficient of determination of 0.997, a low detection limit of about 2.1 Pa, and a response time of about 25 ms, while remaining stable over 6000 loading cycles and 2000 cycles of 50% tensile strain. Building on this single-channel device, we further extend the architecture into a 3-axis gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic force sensor (3-axis GriFIFS) capable of resolving triaxial forces and surface textures. When integrated onto a dexterous robotic hand and combined with a temporal convolutional network, the sensors support tactile object recognition, fabric texture discrimination, human–robot interaction, and tactile-guided assembly, offering a generalizable route to tactile sensing for embodied intelligence.

articles_hidden.title: Sustainable biobased packaging via integrated robotics/machine learning workflow for improved postharvest preservation
articles_hidden.authors: Yang Li, Tianle Chen, Peihua Ma, Tsai-Chun Chung, Bin Zhou, Lianping Wu, Archit R. Golatkar, Shahnaz Mukta, Joshua M. Little, Hayden C. Whitley, Yaguang Luo, Qin Wang, Greg Curtzwiler, Liangbing Hu, Teng Li, Po-Yen Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: Reliance on petroleum-derived plastic packaging exacerbates environmental burdens and lacks intrinsic antimicrobial protection against food spoilage. While biobased materials offer a sustainable alternative, optimizing their formulations is hindered by vast component libraries, inefficient trial-and-error experimentation, and complex multiproperty requirements. Herein, we develop an integrated workflow combining robotic automation, machine learning predictions, density functional theory, and life cycle assessment to accelerate biobased packaging discovery. Leveraging data augmentation and ensemble modeling, we use a hierarchical neural network to predict ∼1 billion candidate formulations, balancing mechanical properties, optical transparency, and environmental footprint. The resulting biobased packaging demonstrates enhanced hydrostability, effective antimicrobial activity, and high barrier performance, significantly extending the shelf life of cucumbers and avocados. Last, we release a data-sharing platform featuring forward prediction, inverse design, and environmental impact functions to support community use. This integrative framework provides sustainable, antimicrobial packaging materials alternative to conventional plastic films.

articles_hidden.title: Fire at the boundary: Airborne toxic metals from the 2025 Los Angeles urban firestorm
articles_hidden.authors: Haroula D. Baliaka, Ryan X. Ward, Sean M. Raffuse, Bradley Ries, Yumeng Cui, Dien Wu, Ruizhe Liu, Can Barut, Sina Hasheminassab, François L. H. Tissot, Armistead G. Russell, John H. Seinfeld, Richard C. Flagan, Roya Bahreini, Paul O. Wennberg, Nga L. Ng
articles_hidden.abstract: Urban fire smoke is chemically distinct from wildland fire smoke yet remains poorly understood. Using real-time airborne trace element measurements during the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton urban firestorm, we show that the plume evolved rapidly as fire transitioned from structures to wildland, tracked hourly by the potassium-to-lead ratio. Compared to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched more than 50-fold in lead, 7-fold in halogens, and 3-fold in arsenic, a toxic mixture linked to burning vehicles, electronics, and building materials, a fundamentally different fuel from conventional wildland vegetation. During peak structural burning, we estimate that approximately 7 million residents (range, 4.3 to 8.0 million) experienced 24-hour lead concentrations exceeding 50 nanograms per cubic meter, over 80 times background levels. Unlike wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume represents an emerging class of urban fire air pollution that demands revised exposure frameworks and emergency response protocols as fires increasingly burn into cities.

articles_hidden.title: Morphological intelligence for dynamic aerial interactions
articles_hidden.authors: Yongkang Jiang, Junjin Li, Shuyu Meng, Yanmin Zhou, Bin He, Jamie Paik
articles_hidden.abstract: Biological flyers achieve ecological dominance not through flight alone, but by seamlessly integrating aerial locomotion with forceful physical interactions, including snatching prey, perching on irregular surfaces, and operating across diverse media. Translating this agility into aerial robotics demands reconciling a fundamental conflict: impulsive, high-force actions destabilize the flight platform. Here, we present a bio-inspired unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a mechanically intelligent impulsive limb that resolves this tradeoff through physical decoupling. An asymmetric bistable impulse module delivers a 2.3-fold extension within 70 ms, while a soft-linkage architecture reduces the transmission of impulsive interaction forces to the airframe. For the tested seven-segment configuration, intrinsic geometric tolerance corresponds to a passive vertical accommodation range of approximately 70% of the fully deployed arm length, reducing the need for precise altitude regulation within the tested range. We demonstrate the system’s multimodal capacity through dynamic in-flight snatching, energy-efficient perching, high-impact solid fracture, and cross-medium capture in viscous fluids, establishing a new paradigm for UAVs executing physically demanding tasks in complex environments.

articles_hidden.title: RAF isoform selectivity of MEK inhibitors and rational design of a covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor
articles_hidden.authors: Sayan Chakraborty, Jie Jiang, Javier Vinals Camallonga, Dimitris Gazgalis, Thomas W. Gero, Maurício T. Tavares, Georgia Dittemore, Emre Tkacik, Tyler S. Beyett, Dong Man Jang, Byung Hak Ha, Felix H. Gottlieb, Talya Levitz, Rebecca J. Metivier, Anna M. Schmoker, David A. Scott, Hyesung Jeon, Pasi A. Jänne, Michael J. Eck
articles_hidden.abstract: Aberrant activation of the RAS/RAF/mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)/extracellular signal–regulated kinase pathway is a frequent cause of cancer. Allosteric MEK inhibitors block this pathway by binding RAF-MEK complexes to prevent activation of MEK by RAF. However, how MEK inhibitor potency varies across the three RAF isoforms remains poorly understood. We profiled seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and observed a notable hierarchy of sensitivity: All most potently inhibited CRAF-driven MEK activation while relatively sparing ARAF-driven activation. We identified point mutations in ARAF and CRAF proximate to the MEK inhibitor binding site that markedly altered inhibitor sensitivity. Using a rational design approach, we developed a more potent inhibitor of ARAF-driven MEK signaling, TWG-07-148. Our cryo–electron microscopy structure shows how this acrylamide-containing analog of MEK inhibitor trametinib covalently targets Cys 514 , a residue unique to ARAF. Our studies highlight the importance of the activating RAF isoform as a determinant of MEK inhibitor sensitivity and provide proof of concept for the development of MEK inhibitors that more effectively block ARAF-driven MEK signaling via covalent targeting of Cys 514 .

articles_hidden.title: Machine psychology for language models
articles_hidden.authors: Thilo Hagendorff, Ishita Dasgupta, Marcel Binz, Stephanie Chan, Andrew Lampinen, Jane X. Wang, Zeynep Akata, Eric Schulz
articles_hidden.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a “machine psychology” for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.

articles_hidden.title: StSIRT1 regulates potato dormancy through deacetylation of peroxidase-like 3 at K37
articles_hidden.authors: Qiannan Hu, Yingying Dong, Hongxia Hu, Yizhou Xiang, Bailin Liu, Tuck-Whye Wong, Zhaojun Ban, Zisheng Luo, Li Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Plants have evolved sophisticated defense systems to synchronize growth with environmental fluctuations, including the adaptive strategy of dormancy, an important agronomic trait. Nevertheless, the role of posttranslational modification of nonhistone proteins in dormancy regulation remains elusive. Here, we report that sirtuin (StSIRT1)–mediated deacetylation of peroxidase (StPRX3) suppresses peroxidase activity, culminating in potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.) dormancy release. The lysine deacetylase StSIRT1—suppressed by the dormancy regulator nicotinamide (NAM)—accumulates during dormancy release and negatively modulates StPRX3. Furthermore, lysine-37 (K37; K denotes lysine) in StPRX3 is essential for its direct interaction with StSIRT1. StSIRT1 interacts with StPRX3 to regulate the hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 )–scavenging capacity of peroxidase by decreasing K37 acetylation levels. Notably, the StPRX3 K37R (K37→arginine, K37R; R denotes arginine) mutant suppresses peroxidase activity, leading to accelerated potato dormancy release. Our findings uncover an StSIRT1-StPRX3 cascade in dormancy regulation that activates peroxidase and reduces H 2 O 2 levels in potato, providing insights into the complex regulatory networks involved in dormancy.

articles_hidden.title: Transient absorption signatures of asymmetric carrier cooling in semiconductors
articles_hidden.authors: Ivan Maliyov, Piotr Jan Kabacinski, Hemen Hosseini, Thomas F. K. Weatherley, Artur Tuktamyshev, Stefano Sanguinetti, Nicolas Grandjean, Stefano Dal Conte, Marco Bernardi, Giulio Cerullo
articles_hidden.abstract: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. Our work shows a predictive experiment-theory framework for understanding the individual dynamics of excited electron and hole carriers, with broad implications for conventional and quantum materials.

articles_hidden.title: Momentum quantization of hyperbolic phonon polaritons in photonic-crystal cavity
articles_hidden.authors: Hwi Je Woo, Heejin Choi, Piyali Biswas, Seonyeong Kim, Hansung Kim, Sunae Seo, Suyong Jung, Eun Seong Lee, Junghoon Jahng, Chang-Won Lee
articles_hidden.abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in van der Waals crystals enable extreme electromagnetic confinement and access to exceptionally large in-plane momenta, offering a powerful platform for deep-subwavelength nanophotonics. Although the lower Reststrahlen band (RS1) of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly attractive for low-loss, strongly volume-confined polaritons, fully exploiting this potential remains challenging because RS1 modes are weakly accessible by conventional near-field detection and require efficient leakage suppression for high-Q confinement. Here, we demonstrate that momentum quantization of RS1 HPhPs enables high-Q, ultrasmall mode volume cavity states in an h-BN photonic-crystal nanocavity architecture. Periodic lateral cavity boundaries impose Fabry-Pérot phase matching, while the surrounding photonic-crystal lattice suppresses in-plane leakage and stabilizes discrete cavity-supported momentum states, transforming the continuous hyperbolic dispersion into a ladder of geometry-defined momentum eigenstates. Using photo-induced force microscopy, we directly visualize the quantized cavity modes in real space and reconstruct their discretized dispersion in momentum space. The resulting hyperbolic polaritonic cavity crystal exhibits quality factors exceeding 340 and ultrasmall mode volumes down to V ¯ m = 4.3 × 10 − 7   ( λ 0 / n ) 3 , corresponding to Purcell enhancements approaching 10 7 . This approach establishes a route to high-Q, ultrasmall-volume RS1 polaritonic nanocavities with geometry-defined momentum states, providing a scalable platform for enhanced light-matter interactions, selective vibrational spectroscopy, and reconfigurable mid-infrared nanophotonic devices.

articles_hidden.title: Interferon-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells protects against congenital Zika virus infection
articles_hidden.authors: Margaret R. Dedloff, Thomas R. Reinhardt, Tessa-Jonne F. Ropp, Joel Rivera-Cardona, Celeste R. Robles, Rebecca L. Casazza, J. Ashley Ezzell, Michelle S. Itano, Helen M. Lazear
articles_hidden.abstract: Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor ( Ifnar1 −/− ) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors ( Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− ) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection in Ifnar1 −/− dams compared to Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus of Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− dams compared to Ifnar1 −/− dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ–responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

articles_hidden.title: Death receptors regulate entry to therapy-induced senescence and orchestrate addiction to IAPs
articles_hidden.authors: Gokhan Gunay, Seren Hamsici, Vaishnavi Venugopalan, Aoife Costigan, Melanie Fritsch, Aislinn Gallagher Aldave, Anne Huber, Brianna Fernandez, Hande Efe-Cicek, Pavel Davidovich, Pavitha Parathan, Akash Srivaths, Natalie Hudson, Eleanor Noone, Jeffrey O’Callaghan, Lisa A. Mielke, Sarah L. Doyle, Sabrina L. Spencer, Matthew Campbell, Conor J. Kearney, Hamid Kashkar, Seamus J. Martin
articles_hidden.abstract: Cytotoxic chemotherapy typically results in the elimination of a fraction of the tumor with surviving cells entering a state of persistence or premature replicative senescence that can lead to recurrence. Here, we show that therapy-induced senescence is associated with robust up-regulation of Fas and/or TRAIL-R2/DR5 death receptors in vitro and in vivo. The latter receptors restricted entry to senescence and exerted selective pressure on senescent cells through promoting assembly of proapoptotic receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD)/Caspase-8 “FADDosome” complexes, restrained by cFLIP L . Accordingly, deletion of CASP-8 robustly enhanced entry to senescence and prolonged the life span of senescent cells. cIAP-2, which inhibits death receptor–driven cell death, was also up-regulated in senescent cells, and deletion of IAPs suppressed entry to senescence. Consistent with this, small-molecule IAP antagonists exhibited potent senolytic activity through enhancing death receptor–initiated Caspase-8 activation. Thus, death receptor–driven assembly of RIPK1/FADD/Caspase-8 complexes in senescent cells orchestrates addiction to IAPs that can be exploited by IAP antagonists.

articles_hidden.title: In situ CAR-M engineered by liposomal mRNA nanomedicine remodels fibrotic microenvironment for ameliorating liver fibrosis
articles_hidden.authors: Hong Xiao, Xiaoxia Li, Kaimin Cai, Yifei Leng, Xiaoyan Miao, Tinghui Yin, Xintao Shuai, Jie Ren
articles_hidden.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a severe complication of diverse chronic liver diseases characterized by a dysregulated hepatic microenvironment, and effective clinical therapeutic strategies for this condition remain lacking to date. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR-Ms) hold considerable therapeutic potential for liver fibrosis via antigen-specific recognition and efferocytotic activity, yet their clinical translation is largely hindered by the sophisticated ex vivo preparation procedures. Herein, we report an in situ CAR-M engineering strategy that uses a phosphatidylserine (PS)–incorporated, macrophage-targeted lipid nanoparticle (LNP) for the codelivery of CAR messenger RNA (mRNA) and Cas9 mRNA in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that this engineered LNP achieves efficient targeting of liver-resident macrophages. Transfection with fibroblast activation protein α (FAPα)–CAR mRNA equips macrophages with the capacity to specifically target activated hepatic stellate cells (aHSCs), whereas Cas9-mediated follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL-1) gene editing enhances the efferocytotic function of macrophages in liver tissues. Consequently, functional CAR-Ms are generated in situ, which elicits robust antifibrotic effects, including reduced collagen deposition, restored sinusoidal architecture and enhanced immune-mediated antifibrotic activity. Collectively, our customized LNP-mediated in situ engineering of liver macrophages into CAR-Ms enables precise antifibrotic intervention for liver fibrosis and circumvents the cumbersome ex vivo CAR-M preparation process.

articles_hidden.title: Nanomaterial-genetics enables near-infrared-driven genetically targeted neuromodulation
articles_hidden.authors: Yi Liu, Xiaolei Wang, Weiwei Yin, Jiahui Chen, Yu Fan, Jiani Yang, Yu Wang, Lin Ge, Wei Rao, Laiyuan Wang, Cheng Li, Zengcai V. Guo, Nan Liu, Xuyang Sun, Yaxiong Yang
articles_hidden.abstract: Stimuli-responsive nanomaterials offer powerful capabilities for neuromodulation, yet there is a continuous need for more versatile methods to ensure cell-specific targeting, a prerequisite for their precise application in neuroscience. To address this gap, we introduce the nanomaterial-genetics (NMG) system, a strategy that integrates genetically encoded synthetic receptors with ligand-functionalized nanoparticles to achieve receptor-guided, cell-selective targeting. Neurons are engineered to express an NMG Receptor carrying an extracellular HaloTag, which selectively captures HaloTag ligand–functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNP-Ligands). This genetically encoded receptor-ligand pairing enables efficient and localized nanomaterial-mediated photothermal activation under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation at ultralow nanoparticle doses, whereas receptor-negative neurons remain largely unresponsive. Receptor-guided targeting substantially reduces nanomaterial-associated cytotoxicity under the tested conditions while preserving robust neuromodulatory efficacy. We demonstrate genetically targeted activation of neurons in vitro and in vivo, including transcranial NIR modulation of mouse locomotor behavior. Collectively, the NMG system offers an extensible complement to current neuromodulation technologies, providing a versatile platform for multimodal and precision neuromodulation.

articles_hidden.title: The structural history of Eukarya
articles_hidden.authors: Diandra Daumiller, Qiuzhen Li, Patrick Bryant
articles_hidden.abstract: Comparative genomics has traditionally relied on sequence-based markers, yet the global evolutionary landscape of protein architecture remains largely unexplored. We present the Structural History of Eukarya (SHE), a structural similarity-derived phylogeny from all-vs-all structural comparisons on the proteome level of 1542 eukaryotic species, encompassing nearly 300 trillion pairwise protein alignments. This proteome-scale analysis reveals a bipartite model of eukaryotic evolution: a rigid Strict Core dominated by cytoskeletal architecture, supporting a more plastic Operational Engine centered on translational machinery. We identify lineage-specific accelerations of structural evolution in species such as birds and ants that are decoupled from proteome expansion. Finally, we demonstrate that proteome-wide structural fidelity enables the functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins and a data-driven framework for model organism selection, replacing heuristic choices with quantitative matching to human biological processes. SHE is freely accessible as an interactive portal.

articles_hidden.title: Glucose restriction induced by intermittent fasting promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to memory CD8 + T cell development
articles_hidden.authors: Da-Jeong Park, Young-Jun Ju, Young Jin Pyung, Cheol Gyun Kim, Narae Kim, MinJi Lim, Hyungseok Seo, Seung Hyun Han, Jae-Ho Cho, Cheol-Heui Yun
articles_hidden.abstract: Dietary restrictions are increasingly recognized as modulators of immune cell function. However, how they shape CD8 + T cell fate decisions remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the impact of intermittent fasting (IF) on differentiation of heterogeneous effector T cell subsets and the formation of a long-lived homeostatic memory pool. We found that IF skewed CD8 + T cell differentiation toward memory precursor effector cells (MPECs) and enhanced the central memory CD8 + T cell development and functions. Mechanistically, glucose restriction induced by IF promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to fatty acid oxidation. This metabolic shift enhanced mitochondrial fitness and supported MPEC differentiation via metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk, culminating in durable and functionally robust memory CD8 + T cell responses. Applying this strategy in adoptive transfer therapy, intratumoral defects could be circumvented by imprinting a memory phenotype under IF-mimicking conditions, resulting in improved and long-lasting antitumor activity. Collectively, these findings underscore the importance of IF in orchestrating metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk to enhance memory formation and antitumor immunity.

articles_hidden.title: Early Gravettian genomic data from Western Europe reveal population movements before the LGM
articles_hidden.authors: Pere Gelabert, Susanna Sawyer, Vanessa Villalba-Mouco, Olivia Cheronet, Victoria Oberreiter, Diego Gárate, Christian Normand, Lawrence G. Straus, Manuel R. González Morales, Igor Gutiérrez-Zugasti, David Cuenca-Solana, Joëlle Darricau, Henry de Lumley, José-Miguel Tejero, Mareike Stahlschmidt, Thomas Higham, Maddalena Giannì, Laura G. van der Sluis, Carla Gómez-Montes, Miriam Ibáñez-Herranz, Michelle Hämmerle, Brina Zagorc, Florian Exler, Florian Brück, Stefan Franz, Fernanda Tenorio Cano, Kristin Stewardson, Lijun Qiu, Ana B. Marín-Arroyo, Michaela Lucci, Alessia Nava, Francesco Genchi, Donato Coppola, Chiara La Marca, Alfredo Coppa, David Reich, Ron Pinhasi
articles_hidden.abstract: Anatomically modern humans first settled in Europe at least 45,000 years ago, yet limited genomic data from 45 to 20 thousand years (ka) constrain reconstructions of Upper Palaeolithic population dynamics. Before the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM; ∼26.5 to 19 ka), Gravettian groups (∼34 to 25 ka) were widespread across Europe and genetically diverse, including the Fournol and Věstonice lineages. Here, we present genome-wide data from three Gravettian individuals: two from the Franco-Cantabrian region (Chufín, Spain, and Isturitz, France) and one from Italy (Ostuni1b). Our analyses reveal previously undetected gene flow between eastern and western early Gravettian populations in southwestern Europe, challenging models of regional genetic continuity from the Aurignacian to the Solutrean (∼24 to 19 ka). To investigate population history during the LGM, a period for which human skeletal remains are extremely rare, we analyzed sedimentary ancient DNA from Solutrean Layer 122 at El Mirón Cave (Cantabria, Spain; ∼22,000 calibrated years before the present), recovering ∼14,000 human single-nucleotide polymorphisms. These data support persistence of Fournol-related ancestry in southwestern Europe throughout the LGM.

articles_hidden.title: Depressed chemical weathering inhibited climate stabilization after the end-Permian biocrisis
articles_hidden.authors: Guang-Yi Wei, Feifei Zhang, Hua Zhang, Yi-Bo Lin, Yi-Sheng Yin, Mohammad N. Gorgij, Sakineh Arefifard, Thomas J. Algeo, Philip A. E. Pogge von Strandmann, Benjamin J. W. Mills, Shu-zhong Shen
articles_hidden.abstract: The Permian-Triassic transition (∼252 million years ago) marks the most severe mass extinction in Earth’s history, followed by a protracted interval of environmental instability and delayed biological recovery. Although elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from extensive volcanism is widely invoked, the role of continental weathering feedbacks in regulating global climate has not been effectively constrained. Here, we present high-resolution lithium isotope records from marine carbonates and terrestrial deposits through the Permian-Triassic transition. Combined with an Earth-system model, our data reveal notable decreases in global continental weatherability following the end-Permian mass extinction, inferred to associations with widespread deforestation (extinction of deep-rooted plants) and the collapse of terrestrial ecosystem. This diminished weathering response to volcanic carbon emissions likely contributed to prolonged high atmospheric CO 2 and global temperature during the Early Triassic. The sustained greenhouse conditions, in turn, inhibited contemporaneous marine and terrestrial ecosystem recoveries. Our findings highlight the importance of terrestrial ecosystem in modulating global carbon cycle stability, and its effects on Earth’s habitability.

articles_hidden.title: Trans-synaptic interaction of orphan GPCR GPR88 and adhesion GPCR BAI3 through C1ql1 maintains synapse integrity
articles_hidden.authors: Ying Han, Qingbiao Meng, Xuan Li, Qin Huang, Liming Qin, Liangyu Liao, Ke-Ke Xing, Jie Cheng, Lulu Guo, Chao Zhang, Tao Chen, Zhiyi Wei, Xiao Yu, Jin-Peng Sun, Bo Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: GPR88 is an orphan GPCR with genetic variants associated with multiple neuropsychiatric conditions. GPR88 exhibits enriched expression in the striatum, olfactory tubercle, and inferior olive. Despite these functional associations, its endogenous ligand and its downstream molecular pathways remain unresolved. Here, we found that climbing fiber (CF)–localized GPR88 regulates CF-Purkinje cell synapses in the cerebellum and associative learning behaviors. The results support the CF-secreted protein C1ql1 as the ligand of GPR88 and further revealed that C1ql1 activates biased Gq signaling to enhance CF synapses. Last, we demonstrated that GPR88 anchors C1ql1 and, via C1ql1, forms a tripartite complex with the postsynaptic adhesion GPCR BAI3 in vitro. These findings resolve the orphan status of GPR88 and likely reveal a mechanism by which a secreted protein links two GPCRs to fine-tune synaptic signaling at pre- and postsynaptic sites.

articles_hidden.title: Bioinspired ventral-groove fibers for volume-programmable pneumatic actuation
articles_hidden.authors: Xiaoyu Zhang, Qianyi Li, Xiaolong Li, Ziang Li, Haoran Qiu, Shiyun Qian, Ying Yi Tan, Hong Yee Low, Tural Khudiyev
articles_hidden.abstract: Pneumatic actuation plays a central role in soft robotics, with conventional systems relying on pressure-driven chamber deformation and closed-loop feedback for precise control. Here, we introduce bioinspired ventral-groove filamentary fibers that reframe pneumatic actuation from pressure-dominated chambers to volume-programmable fiber architectures, enabling previously unexplored robotic capabilities. Coupling microgroove unfolding with elastic expansion, these molecularly programmed fibers achieve reversible 400× area expansion at ultralow pressure (∼0.8 kPa) and scale from ∼100 μm to centimeter-scale diameters and tens of meters in length, supporting micro- to macro-scale robotic systems. We demonstrate responsive textile actuation through an everyday flotation garment with 20-m fibers seamlessly integrated into clothing. We also show a gripping approach with three capabilities: disturbance-robust high-precision grasping, conformal handling of fragile nerve-like filaments and delicate incense-ash cones, and open-loop operation that reduces reliance on sensory feedback. By establishing a volume-programmable actuation paradigm, this work paves the way for low-pressure pneumatic technologies in soft robotics and responsive textiles.

articles_hidden.title: Spider-inspired bidirectional robotic joints driven by electrohydraulic multiaxial strain
articles_hidden.authors: Zean Yuan, Shuhong Huang, Luna Zhou, Xinyu Zhu, Jun Luo, Guo Zhan Lum, Rui Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: Compared with conventional motors and servos, soft-actuated angular-motion devices are superior in environmental adaptability and human-robot interaction, yet they can only achieve active bidirectional angular motion by integrating antagonistic actuators or restriction modules. The integration of such components introduces deformation antagonism, compromises structural simplicity, and increases control complexity. Herein, we propose a spider-inspired centimeter-scale soft bidirectional robotic joint driven by a pair of synchronously controlled electrohydraulic actuators (EHAs). Specifically, the EHAs generate multiaxial strain, enabling the joint to bidirectionally rotate depending on its physical state, without introducing additional functional components or asynchronous controllers. Furthermore, the joint demonstrates (i) high-speed (forward: 2851° per second, reverse: 1934° per second) and wide-stroke (up to 156.8°) rotational performance, (ii) multimodal motion (e.g., self-unfolding, self-folding, and reciprocating swinging), (iii) continuous response (up to 40 hertz), and (iv) payload-bearing capability. Last, three joint-integrated devices validate its feasibility as a multifunctional, high-dynamic, and single-channel-controlled actuation component in diverse robotic applications. This work establishes a viable design framework for minimalist yet versatile bioinspired robots.

articles_hidden.title: A self-powered finger-worn wireless tracking interface for human-machine interaction
articles_hidden.authors: Kaixian Li, Lirong Tang, Siqi Gong, Chuncai Shan, Shuyan Xu, Shaokun Gong, Tingyu Wang, Cuilin Zhang, Yi Xi, Xue Wang, Chenguo Hu, Hengyu Guo
articles_hidden.abstract: Continuous touch positioning and trajectory tracking are essential for immersive human-machine interaction, yet conventional interfaces are fundamentally limited by rigid power supplies and tethered data transmission. Here, we present a completely self-powered, finger-worn interface that wirelessly transmits spatial trajectory data driven solely by biomechanical motion. The device integrates a miniaturized (3.7 cm 2 ) corona-discharge triboelectric nanogenerator with a flexible electromagnetic transmitter, converting multidirectional fingertip movement directly into wireless communication signals. By coupling these signals with three non-collinear receivers and a machine-learning-assisted decoding algorithm, the system achieves sub-millimeter localization accuracy (<0.9 mm). We demonstrate the interface’s capability for the high-fidelity reconstruction of handwritten inputs, enabling robust human-machine control. By synergizing motion-energy harvesting with precise spatial tracking, this work offers an untethered, self-contained paradigm for next-generation interactive intelligent systems.

articles_hidden.title: Polycomb factor PHF19 affects AML initiation, patient prognosis, and survival
articles_hidden.authors: Gianni Paolo Gamarra Figueroa, Arantxa Gutierrez, Enrique Blanco, Pedro Vizán, Cecilia Ballaré, Aleksandra Sparavier, Marta Tosto, Saverio Minucci, Lars Velten, Luciano Di Croce
articles_hidden.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is marked by unchecked expansion of undifferentiated myeloid cells. Although oncogenic fusions such as MLL-AF9 can initiate disease, the early steps of leukemogenesis and the role of cell-intrinsic regulators remain unclear. We previously showed that the Polycomb-associated factor Phf19 is required for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) maintenance and state control in mice and that its loss (Phf19 KO ) impairs HSC function. To define Phf19’s role in transformation, we expressed MLL-AF9 in Phf19 KO hematopoietic cells and performed integrated multiomic analyses. Phf19 deletion promoted acquisition of stemlike features and reduced responsiveness to differentiation-inducing AML therapies. Molecular and functional consequences of Phf19 loss paralleled those observed in the datasets of patients with AML. From these data, we derived a prognostic signature—PHFScore—which reveals previously unrecognized AML survival-correlating genes that robustly stratify patients across distinct cellular origins and leukemogenic stages, underscoring Phf19’s key role in AML biology and prognosis.

articles_hidden.title: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon
articles_hidden.authors: Wenqing Shi, Xiangyu Min, Ziqian Li, Kun Shi, Lin Zhu, Qingji Zhang, Hans W. Paerl, Erik Jeppesen, Boqiang Qin
articles_hidden.abstract: Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO 2 or CH 4 during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. Thus, relying solely on dammed reservoir observations to assess these emissions may introduce considerable bias. Here, we simulated both dammed and non-dammed scenarios for 5346 global reservoir dams to assess their impact on carbon emissions from retained OC. The results show that reservoir-only approaches overestimate dam-induced carbon emissions by neglecting baseline emissions under no-dam conditions. After baseline correction, dams increase carbon emissions by an average of 21.5% in CO 2 -equivalent (CO 2 -eq), which represents only 18.6% of the emissions estimated using the conventional reservoir-based accounting approach. XGBoost identified reservoir depth and hydraulic residence time as the primary controls on dam-induced carbon emissions.

articles_hidden.title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons
articles_hidden.authors: James S. Sinclair, Daniela Cortés-Guzmán, Jukka Aroviita, Nathan J. Baker, Libuše Barešová, Catherine Bradley, Miguel Cañedo-Argüelles, David Cunillera-Montcusí, Hugh B. Feeley, Martial Ferréol, Mathieu Floury, Marie Anne Eurie Forio, Peter Goethals, Alexia M. González-Ferreras, Kaisa-Leena Huttunen, Ioannis Karaouzas, Aitor Larrañaga, S. Jannicke Moe, Ariane Moulinec, Diana Osadčaja, Petr Pařil, Andrés Peredo Arce, Marek Polášek, Michal Straka, Rudy Vannevel, Martin Wilkes, Peter Haase
articles_hidden.abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing “impact trajectories”). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

articles_hidden.title: Engineering a closed-loop electrochemical pathway for cadmium recovery and aqueous battery reutilization
articles_hidden.authors: Yue Wang, Nan Zhao, Haobin Song, Yangfeng Cui, Hui Ying Yang
articles_hidden.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) waste is an unavoidable toxic by-product of zinc processing, but its electrochemical reutilization remains limited by the lack of routes that couple selective recovery with stable metal-anode operation. Here, we report a closed-loop electrochemical strategy that transforms model Cd-containing waste electrolytes into regenerable aqueous Cd metal anodes. A three-step potential-programmed electrodeposition process selectively recovers Cd while constructing compact Cd(002)-textured electrodes with tunable areal capacity. To preserve this recovered structure during cycling, cesium iodide is introduced to reconstruct the Cd-electrolyte interface, enabling iodide-dominated and cesium-assisted regulation of desolvation, ion flux, corrosion, and Cd growth. The resulting Cd anode achieves 99.98% average Coulombic efficiency and stable high-rate plating/stripping. Cd||I 2 coin and pouch cells validate full-cell operation under high loading and reduced excess Cd. Failed Cd anodes can be reextracted, regenerated, and reused, completing a recovery-operation-regeneration loop.

articles_hidden.title: PhagoID: Quantitative in situ proximity labeling defines the proteomes of bead- and microbe-containing phagosome lumina across species, maturation, and immune activation
articles_hidden.authors: Benjamin L. Allsup, Supriya Gharpure, Cal Gunnarsson, Mateo L. Stagg, Bryan D. Bryson
articles_hidden.abstract: The phagosome is an immune organelle that integrates signals from diverse cargos to drive pathogen killing, tissue homeostasis, and antigen presentation. How this compartment coordinates such diverse functions remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive view of phagosomal composition across cell states and perturbations could accelerate insight into its regulation. Here, we establish PhagoID, a modular proximity labeling approach that enables in situ proteomic profiling of the phagosome lumen in living cells. Applying PhagoID to murine and human macrophages, we define conserved and species-specific phagosomal proteomes that include both canonical lysosomal components and unexpected contributors from nuclear, mitochondrial, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) compartments. Integrating these proteomes with 25 genome-scale CRISPR screens of phagosomal phenotypes, we identify a network of lumenal proteins that regulate cargo uptake, acidification, antigen presentation, and microbial control highlighting previously unrecognized phagosomal effectors. We next adapt PhagoID to profile the microbe-containing phagosome and compare the sterile bead-containing phagosome to the Escherichia coli –containing phagosome, demonstrating a modest E. coli signature of phagosome remodeling. Comparative analyses further reveal that loss of LAMP1 enhances recruitment of ER-derived proteins to the phagosome, whereas loss of TFEB minimally perturbs the lumenal proteome despite its role in lysosomal biogenesis. Last, cytokine stimulation remodels the phagosome lumen to enrich for proteins involved in antigen presentation and antimicrobial activity in response to type I and II interferons. These data demonstrate that PhagoID delivers a high-confidence, quantitative, and integrative map of the phagosome lumen, revealing previously unidentified axes of organellar communication and regulatory control in innate immunity.

articles_hidden.title: Lineage-specific and gestational age–dependent DNA methylation programming orchestrates human placental development
articles_hidden.authors: Shanru Yi, Jing Xiao, Ruixue Wang, Mengting Wang, Chunyan Le, Guang Yang, Shanshan Yi, Wenju Liu, Hong Wang, Xiaocui Li, Xiaoyu Liu, Kai Wang, Cizhong Jiang, Shaorong Gao, Jiayu Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: The human placenta is essential for pregnancy, yet the dynamic regulation of its DNA methylome during development remains poorly understood. To address this, we generated a single base–resolution DNA methylation atlas of human placental trophoblasts across gestation. We identified a lineage-specific methylation program established immediately after implantation, followed by gestational age–dependent methylation accumulation. This program acted as a developmental barrier that coordinated placental maturation and immune homeostasis. By integrating histone modifications and functional perturbations, we revealed a temporal dynamic between H3K27me3 and DNA methylation that silenced proinflammatory loci and a switch from H3K9me3 to DNA methylation at repeat elements to maintain genome stability. Aberrant methylation in preterm placentas underscored the physiological importance of methylation regulation. Using human trophoblast stem cells, we demonstrated that DNMT1 was critically required for maintaining trophoblast methylome integrity and self-renewal, while the DNMT3 family were equally essential for trophoblast survival. Overall, we established a placenta-specific epigenetic framework for human trophoblast development.

articles_hidden.title: Direct observations of submesoscale turbulence driving mesoscale eddy leakage
articles_hidden.authors: Haijin Cao, Zhiyou Jing, Baylor Fox-Kemper, Bo Qiu, Joseph H. Lacasce, Tong Yan
articles_hidden.abstract: Understanding oceanic transport and material fate has long relied on observations that primarily resolve mesoscale, largely geostrophic flows, leaving the role of submesoscale turbulence comparatively unobserved and poorly understood. Here, using new high-resolution drifter-cluster experiments with closest initial spacings below 1 km, we provide direct Lagrangian observations of how submesoscale turbulence modifies mesoscale eddy coherence and transport pathways. The clustered drifters resolve intense, transient ageostrophic motions that are fundamentally absent from geostrophic descriptions of eddy behavior. Analyzed in an eddy-centered reference frame, the observations reveal pronounced submesoscale-driven radial dispersion that facilitates substantial water-mass exchange between the eddy core and its periphery in both the mixed layer and the subsurface. Quantitative estimates indicate submesoscale horizontal diffusivity of O (10 to 100) m 2 /s and a nonlocal dispersion regime across submesoscales. These results challenge the traditional view of mesoscale eddies as coherent structures containing a persistent water mass, with broad implications for interpreting and predicting the transport and fate of tracers in the ocean.

articles_hidden.title: Structural basis for start codon selection by eIF5-mimic proteins
articles_hidden.authors: Ximena Zottig, Chun-Ying Huang, Zahra Seraj, Nikolaus Grigorieff, Andrei A. Korostelev
articles_hidden.abstract: Start codon selection extensively regulates the cellular proteome and is implicated in cancer and other diseases. The eIF5-mimic proteins (5MPs: 5MP1/BZW2 and 5MP2/BZW2) restrict non-AUG start codon usage and thereby reprogram proteoform expression from mRNAs with alternative start sites, such as the oncogenic c-Myc. Here, using in extracto cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biochemical assays, we report how 5MP represses translation dependent on the sequence context at start codons. Cryo-EM structures of 48 S preinitiation complexes (PICs) reveal 5MP1 bound at the A site of the small ribosomal subunit. 5MPs act as initiation factors that stabilize an open PIC conformation, promoting mRNA scanning and inhibiting initiation at suboptimal start codons. We propose to designate 5MP as eIF1S (eukaryotic initiation factor 1 scanning). These findings reveal the structural basis for proteome modulation by 5MPs and may help correct dysregulated translation in disease.

articles_hidden.title: Scalable architecture for measurement-induced squeezed light interferometers
articles_hidden.authors: Abhinav Verma, Jacob Hastrup, Jonas S. Neergaard-Nielsen, Ulrik L. Andersen
articles_hidden.abstract: Scalable interferometers lie at the heart of photonic quantum technologies, but their expansion has been fundamentally limited by optical losses that grow with circuit depth. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a measurement-induced architecture for multimode squeezed-light interferometers that overcomes this barrier. By shifting complexity from deep optical networks to programmable homodyne measurements, we realize effective transformations within a shallow, low-loss platform. We validate the principle with a six-mode device and extend it to a 400-mode interferometer, marking a leap in scale beyond conventional designs. Crucially, this strategy not only enables scalable squeezed light interferometry but also provides a powerful route to the generation of large-scale entangled states—a key requirement for quantum computing, simulation, and communication. Our results establish measurement-induced circuits as a practical pathway toward noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) applications and future demonstrations of quantum advantage.

articles_hidden.title: Double-layer liquid-surface printing of soft films for flexible electronics
articles_hidden.authors: Mengtian Yin, Ziyu Chen, Boshen Xu, Yue Zhang, Pei Dong, Baoxing Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Soft thin films are essential platforms for developing flexible electronics. However, producing thin films with uniform thickness, free residual stress while often followed by a subsequent defect-free transfer at high yield remains a significant fabrication challenge. Here, we present a liquid-surface printing technique that enables the fabrication of highly uniform, soft, thin films by leveraging controlled spreading of 3D-printed polymeric ink droplets on a double-layer immiscible liquid substrate. The inherent smoothness of the liquid surface together with the self-leveling-driven uniformity of the immiscible liquid layer yields precise control over ink droplet spreading and produces highly uniform soft films free of structural defects or surface irregularities. These films can be programmably transferred onto curvilinear substrates because of the fluidic nature of the underlying liquid substrate and its weak van der Waals interactions with the films while maintaining conformal contact. We demonstrate the versatility of this printing approach by fabricating a broad variety of geometric patterns and local features and also validate its robustness by their extensive mechanical and electrical performance measurement. We further fabricate flexible radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags and conformally deploy them to the “skin” of food or food packaging with diverse curvatures for real-time spoilage monitoring, showcasing this technological capability and potential for fabricating flexible and conformable electronics.

articles_hidden.title: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions
articles_hidden.authors: Chirag Manchanda, Ronald C. Cohen, Ramon A. Alvarez, Tammy M. Thompson, Maria H. Harris, Alexander J. Turner, Julian D. Marshall, Robert A. Harley, Joshua S. Apte
articles_hidden.abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 meters by 150 meters) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. In West Oakland, CA—an overburdened community near major freight infrastructure—our approach identifies underestimated and unaccounted emission sources, increasing estimated BC emissions by ∼33%. These corrections quadruple the contribution of neighborhood and port-related sources to population-weighted exposures (from 5 to 20%), disproportionately affecting low-income neighborhoods adjacent to freight corridors. Our results demonstrate that combining dense observational data with inverse modeling enables detection and quantification of overlooked emissions, supporting targeted intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicate similar performance with a substantially reduced fixed-site network (∼10 monitors; ∼1 site per square kilometer, compared with 6.7 sites per square kilometer in the full campaign), paired with time-averaged mobile maps, supporting applicability in data-limited urban settings.

articles_hidden.title: Engineering bacterial morphology through MreB remodeling enhances one-carbon metabolism for sustainable bioproduction
articles_hidden.authors: Yun Chen, Jiahui Peng, Liang Guo, Zaigao Tan
articles_hidden.abstract: The actin-like cytoskeletal protein MreB controls bacterial cell morphology, yet whether engineered modulation of MreB-associated architecture can improve microbial metabolism remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a chemical-genetic platform in Escherichia coli combining an engineered MreB variant (A53R) that remodels cellular morphology with A22-mediated perturbation of MreB dynamics. MreB(A53R) reshaped cell morphology and engaged an RpoE-Cra-GadE regulatory network associated with cellular adaptation, which remodeled electron transport, redirected carbon flux toward NADPH-generating pathways, and reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). Consequently, engineered strains exhibited enhanced formaldehyde tolerance and efficient assimilation of methanol and other C1 substrates. Acute A22 treatment recapitulated the morphological alteration but failed to induce metabolic rewiring, revealing a two-stage adaptive response involving immediate physical adaptation associated with cell envelope reinforcement and long-term transcription-dependent metabolic adaptation to persistent morphological remodeling. The analogous V45R mutation in the native methylotroph Bacillus methanolicus partially recapitulated the improved C1 utilization phenotype, supporting the transferability of MreB-based morphological engineering. Collectively, these findings establish MreB-mediated morphological engineering as a strategy to couple cellular architecture with central carbon and redox metabolism and provide a framework for engineering robust microbial chassis for C1 bioconversion.

articles_hidden.title: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction
articles_hidden.authors: Susannah C. Herz, Menghan Li, Andrew A. Siciliano, Chadlin M. Ostrander, Sune G. Nielsen, Tapan Mukerji, Stephen E. Grasby, Demir Altiner, Daniel J. Lehrmann, David P. G. Bond, Meiyi Yu, Diego P. Fernandez, Christopher R. Anderson, Jonathan L. Payne, Yanan Shen
articles_hidden.abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth’s history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.

articles_hidden.title: The nonsense-mediated decay RNA-surveillance pathway facilitates the hypoxia response by C. elegans
articles_hidden.authors: Calista Diehl, H. Robert Horvitz
articles_hidden.abstract: Hypoxia (decreased O 2 ) induces physiological, metabolic, and behavioral changes. The major hypoxia response pathway is conserved from nematodes to mammals and is driven by activation of the HIF (hypoxia inducible factor) family of transcription factors. Despite a fundamental role of the HIF pathway in regulating cellular homeostasis in response to hypoxic stress, interactions between the HIF pathway and cellular quality control pathways are largely unknown. Using an unbiased genetic screen, we found that in C. elegans nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), an evolutionarily conserved mechanism of RNA surveillance, acts in parallel to HIF-1 to selectively enhance specific aspects of the response to HIF-1 activation, possibly through coregulation of a distinct subset of HIF-1–up-regulated genes. Our findings reveal a functional integration between oxygen sensing and RNA surveillance and establish NMD as a key regulator of specific aspects of the HIF-1–driven transcriptional program and physiological response.

articles_hidden.title: A methylation-dependent reader couples arginine methylation to S6K2 signaling in vivo
articles_hidden.authors: Yalong Wang, Bin Liu, Rongjie Fu, Wei He, Daniel J. McGrail, Han Xu, Mark T. Bedford
articles_hidden.abstract: Arginine methylation regulates diverse cellular processes, yet how methyl-arginine reader proteins couple this modification to kinase signaling in vivo remains poorly defined. Here, we identify staphylococcal nuclease and Tudor domain containing 1 (SND1) as a pancreas-enriched effector that links symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) recognition to S6 kinase 2 (S6K2) activation. Disruption of SDMA-mediated binding by a point mutation in the SND1 Tudor domain markedly diminishes ribosomal protein S6 (S6) phosphorylation in the pancreas. Mechanistically, SND1 engages SDMA-modified arginines within the carboxyl-terminal glycine-arginine–rich (GAR) motif of S6K2 and promotes S6K2-dependent S6 phosphorylation. Mice harboring lysine substitutions at these GAR arginines ( S6k2 RK) phenocopy Snd1 Tudor-mutant ( Snd1 knock-in) animals, exhibiting impaired pancreatic S6 phosphorylation. Transcriptomic analyses reveal extensive overlap in dysregulated pathways between Snd1 and S6k2 mutant pancreata, supporting a shared signaling cascade. Together, these findings establish a methylation-dependent reader-kinase axis that links protein arginine methyltransferase 5–catalyzed arginine methylation to tissue-specific control of ribosome signaling and cellular stress adaptation.

articles_hidden.title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
articles_hidden.authors: Luigi Ippolito, Erica Pranzini, Giulia Gangarossa, Marta Iozzo, Giuseppina Comito, Giacomo Venditti, Sara Roccabianca, Elisa Pardella, Matteo Lulli, Alice Santi, Gabriella Nesi, Elisa Giannoni, Paola Chiarugi
articles_hidden.abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

articles_hidden.title: Using initial states to identify successful El Niño–Southern Oscillation forecasts 1 year in advance
articles_hidden.authors: Nandini Ramesh, Mandy B. Freund, Damien B. Irving, Dougal T. Squire, Carly R. Tozer, Didier P. Monselesan, Tess Parker, Annette Stellema, James S. Risbey
articles_hidden.abstract: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the primary source of climate predictability on seasonal and longer timescales over much of the globe, but predicting its phase beyond 9 months has remained challenging. Here, we leverage an underappreciated factor in ENSO forecasting: the substantial variation in forecast skill based on the ENSO phase at the time a forecast is issued. Our analysis of transitions between ENSO phases in a dynamical hindcast dataset demonstrates that this variation markedly exceeds intermodel differences in predictive capability. Forecasts initialized during La Niña conditions perform best, with three models correctly predicting transitions to El Niño 1 year in advance over 70% of the time. We present our findings in a simple framework that allows decision-makers to assess the likelihood of a forecast being correct on the basis of the current ENSO state. Applied effectively, these findings could improve long-lead ENSO forecasting strategies, enhancing global risk management.

articles_hidden.title: Opposing cell-type preferences for binding and replication shape influenza A virus infection in human airways
articles_hidden.authors: Josephine von Kempis, Marie O. Pohl, Elisabeth Gaggioli, Cyrille Niklaus, Alexandra Trkola, Geert-Jan Boons, Robert P. de Vries, Silke Stertz
articles_hidden.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type–specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

articles_hidden.title: An in situ forming immunomodulatory hydrogel reinvigorates exhausted CD8 + T cells via preserving their mitochondrial fitness
articles_hidden.authors: Yiming Qi, Jing Li, Ziyan Chen, Chenming Zou, Haichao Zhu, Alice Shen Yi Shan, Yuli Fu, Jingwen Hou, Chaozhu Zheng, Qiongzhe Ren, Yu Qiao, Zhu Jin, Feihu Wang, Shengrong Guo
articles_hidden.abstract: CD8 + T cell exhaustion driven by mitochondrial dysfunction remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy. Here, we report an in situ forming d -α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS)–based hydrogel [multifunctional thermosensitive composite gel (MTC Gel)] that reinvigorates exhausted CD8 + T cells by preserving mitochondrial fitness through a two-pronged strategy. After intratumoral injection, MTC Gel rapidly undergoes gelation at physiological temperature and dissociates to generate a high local concentration of TPGS, which targets cancer cell mitochondria to trigger prodeath mitophagy. This process induces robust immunogenic cell death (ICD) and blocks tunneling nanotube–mediated mitochondrial hijacking. Meanwhile, NLG919-loaded hybrid nanoparticles released from MTC Gel synergistically restore mitochondrial biogenesis in CD8 + T cells suppressed by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1. Across multiple murine tumor models, MTC Gel reprograms T cell immunity by reducing CD8 + T cells exhaustion while enhancing effector and cytotoxic functions, thereby eliciting potent tumoricidal activity. These findings highlight this rationally designed hydrogel system as a clinically translatable platform for next-generation ICD-based cancer immunotherapies.

articles_hidden.title: A systematic pan-cancer analysis of intratumoral microbiota-derived epitopes to inform cancer immunotherapy and prevention
articles_hidden.authors: Donghao Li, Hao Wang, Jiyu Guo, Feng Leng, Xinran Zhi, Manyu Gong, Mengqian Zeng, Kefan Liu, Yuhong Sun, Yongsheng Li, Ying Zhang, Juan Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

articles_hidden.title: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release
articles_hidden.authors: Akanksha Jain, Rico Dong, Jana Kroll, Jack F. Webster, Jon Moss, Arthur Bikbaev, Sila K. Ultanir, Alfredo Gonzalez-Sulser, Christian Rosenmund, Martin Heine, Jian Liu, Michael A. Cousin, Daniela Ivanova
articles_hidden.abstract: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

articles_hidden.title: An innovative colon inflammation-targeting platform for ulcerative colitis treatment
articles_hidden.authors: Waliul Islam, Haiming Chen, Ling Li, Kevan J. Salimian, Florin M. Selaru
articles_hidden.abstract: The therapeutic options for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have recently expanded substantially. Tofacitinib, an oral small-molecule inhibitor of Janus kinase (JAK), recently FDA approved for ulcerative colitis, represented a paradigm shift in a field previously dominated by biologics. Tofacitinib, however, carries a black box warning for major adverse cardiovascular events, an elevated risk of malignancies, risk of blood clots, and pulmonary embolism. In addition, tofacitinib is avoided in pregnancy and used with caution in women of child bearing age due to potential risks to the developing fetus. Notably, these potential complications are all due to the systemic distribution of tofacitinib. To address these issues, we developed Lipo-tm-HA, a liposomal platform incorporating mannitol (m) and hyaluronic acid (HA) for targeting tofacitinib (t) to the inflamed colon. We characterized Lipo-tm-HA and have shown that it (i) remains stable in gastric conditions due to HA coating, (ii) adheres to transferrin in inflamed mucosa due to its negative charge, and (iii) enhances macrophage uptake through mannose receptor–mediated endocytosis. Due to targeting, we show that a single oral administration of Lipo-tm-HA at a dose of 10 milligrams per kilogram is superior in efficacy compared with daily treatment with free tofacitinib in a dextran sodium sulfate–induced colitis model. Collectively, our innovative formulation will enable colonic inflammation targeting, reduce systemic exposure, and allow administration of decreased doses.

articles_hidden.title: Wdr82-COMPASS coordinates Foxp3 and TCR signaling to sustain T reg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation
articles_hidden.authors: Wenjun Huang, Jun Li, Minghong He, Beisi Xu, Wojciech Rosikiewicz, Xiaolei Hao, Menglin Jiang, Lu Bai, Siwei Zhang, Lei Li, Wenjie Qi, Vivek Choudhary, Min-Jhen Jheng, Ti-Cheng Chang, Laura J. Janke, Shondra M. Pruett-Miller, Kiran Kodali, Zuo-Fei Yuan, Anthony A. High, Hongjian Jin, Chunliang Li, Yongqiang Feng
articles_hidden.abstract: Regulatory T cells (T reg cells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by T reg cells versus conventional T cells (T conv cells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS–trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports T reg cell development and function. Although Wdr82 deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell–specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory T conv cell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type T reg cells, indicating a primary defect in T reg cell–mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at T reg cell–associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the T reg cell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains T reg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

articles_hidden.title: Histone methyltransferase NSD2 shapes CD8 + T cell fates through the H3K36me2- Zbtb20 axis
articles_hidden.authors: Shijie Yuan, Yifan Xu, Huicheng Liu, Ying Xue, Mengdi Zhu, Xiaorong Xie, Xuwei Wu, Yuting Xia, Lin Li, Yuan Luo, Zehan Huang, Xiangping Yang, Huiyun Du, Ran He
articles_hidden.abstract: CD8 + T cells, as the most important cytolytic cells in adaptive immunity, can differentiate into distinct subpopulations with specific functions and fates. During this process, CD8 + T cells exhibit substantial plasticity in their differentiation trajectory. Notably, epigenetic regulation has emerged as a pivotal mechanism to govern T cell fate decisions. In this study, we demonstrate that the histone methyltransferase NSD2 critically regulates CD8 + T cell differentiation during acute viral infection. While NSD2 deficiency enhances the early expansion of activated CD8 + T cells, it severely compromises their survival fitness during the contraction phase, leading to a disproportionate collapse of the antigen-specific pool and limiting the establishment of robust long-lived memory. Mechanistically, this defect is driven by the disruption of the H3K36me2- Zbtb20 regulatory axis. Furthermore, we show that in the absence of NSD2, CD8 + T cells in tumor exhibit an increased proportion but dysfunctional resident memory T cell phenotype. Collectively, our findings highlight a critical role for NSD2 in providing more mechanistic insights into how epigenetic mechanisms fine-tune T cell differentiation.

articles_hidden.title: SCML2 inhibits PrimPol-mediated DNA replication repriming and regulates replication gap-associated cancer cell vulnerability
articles_hidden.authors: Xin Shi, Qianqian Peng, Jing Guo, Wei Wu, Ping Wang, Xin Zhou, Qiang Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: PrimPol-mediated fork repriming generates single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gaps during DNA damage tolerance (DDT), which, if not properly repaired, can threaten genomic stability. PrimPol is a highly error-prone polymerase. Thus, PrimPol activity should be tightly regulated to fit into DDT and remain low during unstressed DNA replication. Human sex comb on midleg like-2 (SCML2), a Polycomb protein containing MBT repeats, has been identified as a component of the noncanonical PRC1 complex and a regulator of p53 and CHK1 stability. Here, we show that SCML2A is a suppressor of PrimPol. SCML2A directly binds two domains of PrimPol: Its RBR domain binds the C terminus of PrimPol, and its SAM domain binds the amino-terminal AEP domain, thereby inhibiting ssDNA-binding capacity of the AEP domain. SCML2 depletion leads to increased nascent DNA synthesis and accumulation of PrimPol-mediated ssDNA gaps under replication stress. SCML2 depletion also enhances PrimPol engagement during unstressed DNA replication, leading to subsequent accumulation of ssDNA gaps, which are filled by REV1/POLζ-mediated translesion synthesis (TLS) and RAD51-mediated template switching (TS). SCML2 depletion confers cellular hypersensitivity to RAD51 or REV1/POLζ inhibition, which is associated with increased accumulation of ssDNA gaps. Furthermore, CDK2 phosphorylates SCML2A at Ser 267 , which suppresses RBR-mediated PrimPol interaction. Cyclin E1 overexpression leads to CDK2-mediated SCML2A Ser 267 hyperphosphorylation, which releases the inhibitory effect of SCML2A on PrimPol and subsequently induces ssDNA gap accumulation. Collectively, we identify SCML2A as a negative regulator of PrimPol.

articles_hidden.title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation
articles_hidden.authors: Beihong Ji, Matthew Brock, Yuhui Wu, Yuemin Bian, Xibing He, Yue Liu, Yixuan Hao, Haocheng Tang, Junmei Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification.
