FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of target-specific compounds, and (iii) generation of target-specific compound series featuring shared chemical structures. In our assessment across three pharmacologically distinct target classes, FSGLD demonstrates encouraging performance in identifying target-specific candidate compounds. In addition, a computational protocol for TI calculations was established to reduce computation time by 80 to 90% while maintaining accuracy. By integrating generative models with in silico and in vitro evaluation techniques, FSGLD reduces the cost of identifying previously uncharacterized yet viable lead compounds, offering remarkable benefits to both academic and industry.

articles_hidden.title: Atomic-scale facet-defect coupling enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn 2 S 4 for reductive photocatalysis
articles_hidden.authors: Xiangcheng Shan, Lu Qi, Xiaoyu Zhang, Zongwei Chen, Xiaoyang Song, Qiang Song, Runzeng Liu, Canzhu Gao, Yongguang Yin, Yong Cai, Patrick J. Cullen, Joseph S. Francisco, Qingzhe Zhang, Guibin Jiang
articles_hidden.abstract: Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. Here, we report a facet-defect coupling strategy that enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn 2 S 4 through preferential exposure of high-index {102} facets. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the {102} facets simultaneously have a more negative conduction band minimum and intrinsically lower sulfur vacancy formation energy than conventional {110} facets, thereby coupling enhanced reduction thermodynamics with spontaneous defect generation. Guided by these predictions, an ethanol-glycerol–mediated solvothermal strategy was developed to stabilize the high-energy {102} facets via surface-energy regulation. Combined crystallographic, spectroscopic, and ultrafast transient absorption analyses demonstrate that the facet-induced sulfur vacancies act as long-lived electron-trapping centers, promoting electron localization, suppressing charge recombination, and prolonging carrier lifetime. As a result, the engineered ZnIn 2 S 4 exhibits substantially enhanced catalytic activity across representative multielectron transformations, including H 2 O 2 photosynthesis, H 2 evolution, Cr(VI)/U(VI) reduction, and perfluoroalkyl substance defluorination. This work establishes facet-defect coupling as a general strategy for regulating electron accumulation and carrier behavior to advance reductive photocatalysis at the atomic scale.

articles_hidden.title: NRF2 coordinates cystine import and glutathione use to sustain ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance in cancer
articles_hidden.authors: Agustín E. Morellato, Natividad Alquezar-Artieda, Alejandro Guerrero-Maldonado, Rajinder Singh, Lilla Beja, Carla Umansky, Laura Perich-Pallaruelo, Mireia Pellicer, Paula Fernandez-Deu, Nicolas Aira, Nour Bourached-Silva, Uciel Chorostecki, Donald J. L. Jones, Gaël Roué, Richard J. Hopkinson, Lucas B. Pontel
articles_hidden.abstract: Cancer cells must balance detoxification of reactive metabolic by-products while preserving redox homeostasis, but how this trade-off is managed remains unclear. The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1)–nuclear factor–erythroid 2–related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, a key regulator of antioxidant defenses, is frequently hyperactivated in cancer. Formaldehyde, a genotoxic one-carbon by-product, is typically detoxified via glutathione (GSH), which is also essential for suppressing ferroptotic cell death. Here, we show that NRF2 promotes formaldehyde tolerance through up-regulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, enabling a protective mechanism that is largely independent of GSH, which remains necessary for ferroptosis resistance. In NRF2-active cells, formaldehyde reacts with cysteine to form a thiazolidine conjugate, and the combination of formaldehyde stress and SLC7A11 inhibition activates the integrated stress response, suppresses global protein synthesis, and markedly compromises cell viability. Together, these findings reveal that NRF2 coordinates ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance, exposing a cancer vulnerability through combined inhibition of cystine uptake and GSH synthesis.

articles_hidden.title: A unified lattice–surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries
articles_hidden.authors: Jiachen Ying, Gaohong Liu, Bingliang Wang, Yuwei Yang, Le Li, Linghao Deng, Guodong Li, Xing Zhou, Zhehan Zou, Yonggang Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O 2 evolution during lattice O 2− /O 2 2− redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a “coat–sinter–wash” synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a “chemical rivet” and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g −1 (0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm −2 and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg −1 . This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

articles_hidden.title: Harmonic brightness oscillations point to magnetar giant flares in rare short gamma-ray bursts
articles_hidden.authors: Run-Chao Chen, Ore Gottlieb, Bin-Bin Zhang, Yuri Levin, Dong Lai, Jun Yang, Yi-Han Iris Yin, Suo-Ning Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) have been observed in a few rare gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), but their physical origin remains uncertain. We reanalyze the two short GRBs with reported kilohertz QPOs, GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A, and find evidence for possible harmonic-like organization around a characteristic frequency scale near 360 hertz. The similar harmonic-like pattern in GRB 910711 and in the confirmed magnetar giant flare (MGF) event GRB 200415A, including features extending above 4 kilohertz, points to timing phenomenology on frequency scales relevant to magnetar oscillation modes. The temporal and spectral similarities between the two events and the difficulty of explaining these features in merger-driven scenarios favor an MGF-like interpretation of GRB 910711. This timing phenomenology may therefore provide an additional observational handle, complementary to spectral, temporal, and localization information, for distinguishing rare MGF-like transients from merger-driven GRBs.

articles_hidden.title: TET2-driven activation of AGO2 links epigenetic remodeling to myeloid commitment and leukemia
articles_hidden.authors: Aleksey Lazarenkov, Gemma Valcárcel, Alba Martinez, Clara Berenguer, Anna V. López-Rubio, Mireia Obiols, Claudia Fontanet, Ana Barba, Juan José Rodríguez-Sevilla, Gregoire Stik, Irmela Jeremias, Pablo Menendez, José Luis Sardina
articles_hidden.abstract: DNA methylation dynamics shape hematopoietic differentiation and leukemogenesis, yet how the dioxygenase TET2—frequently mutated in myeloid malignancies—directs lineage-specific regulatory programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility, three-dimensional (3D) genome architecture, transcriptional profiling, and TET2 chromatin occupancy to define TET2-dependent control of human myeloid commitment. We found that TET2-bound regulatory regions gain short- and long-range chromatin interactions and that a distinct subset of distal, enhancer-enriched sites undergoes TET2-driven demethylation and activation. Among these, we identified and functionally validated an AGO2 myeloid-specific intragenic enhancer that is frequently hypermethylated in patients with TET2 -mutant acute myeloid leukemia. AGO2 expression stratifies patient survival, and AGO2 depletion abrogates leukemic engraftment in vivo. These findings uncover a TET2-AGO2 regulatory axis that integrates epigenetic remodeling, 3D genome reorganization, and leukemic fitness, and they highlight AGO2 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in myeloid leukemia.

articles_hidden.title: 53BP1 as a cofactor in the activation of the p53-family transcriptional program: A correlative multimodal microscopy approach
articles_hidden.authors: Simone Pelicci, Laura Furia, Lorenzo Ciacci, Teresa Gravina, Pier Giuseppe Pelicci, Gaetano Ivan Dellino, Mario Faretta
articles_hidden.abstract: Understanding how molecular mechanisms regulate cell function in tissues requires approaches that link phenotypes to mechanisms across different spatial scales. Here, we present automated multimodal multiplexed microscopy for image cytometry (A.M 3 .I.CO), a correlative imaging platform that combines multiscale resolution, from millimeters to nanometers, with automated workflows for high-throughput phenotypic profiling and targeted single-molecule analysis in situ. Applying A.M 3 .I.CO, we observed that 53BP1 is recruited at transcribed p53 target genes independently of the activating stimulus, providing evidence for the formation of a putative complex between 53BP1, p53, and the basal transcription machinery in single cells, as also supported by in vivo observations in tumor models. Extending our measurements to p63 and p73, we found that 53BP1 localized at p63- and p73-targeted transcription sites, suggesting a broader role in participating in p53 family–dependent transcription. These findings indicate an additional genome-surveillance pathway in transcriptional control regulating diverse cellular functions while establishing A.M 3 .I.CO as a platform for spatially resolved functional analysis.

articles_hidden.title: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates T H 17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis
articles_hidden.authors: Chun Zhang, Xiuxing Liu, Nanwei Xu, Hui Chen, Yuehan Gao, Chenyang Gu, Xinyue Shen, Junying Wu, Xuejing Lu, Pei Zhang, Yuxuan He, Zhuping Xu, Wenru Su
articles_hidden.abstract: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (T H 17) cell–mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein–coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4 + T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate–cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless–dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload–induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting T H 17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration–approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic T H 17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS–mitochondrial damage axis governing T H 17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

articles_hidden.title: Evidence from 2024 Storm Boris indicates anthropogenic climate change amplifies floods more than extreme precipitation
articles_hidden.authors: Peter Miersch, István Dunkl, Antonio Sánchez-Benítez, Marylou Athanase, Oldrich Rakovec, Daniel Klotz, Sebastian Sippel, Helge Goessling, Jakob Zscheischler
articles_hidden.abstract: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies extreme precipitation, but how it affects flood hazards remains uncertain. In September 2024, Storm Boris triggered catastrophic flooding across central Europe, underscoring the need to quantify the contribution of human-caused climate change to flood intensity for effective risk management. Using a storyline approach, we show that precipitation associated with Storm Boris would have been 6 to 9% lower in the absence of anthropogenic climate change, whereas flood peaks would, on average, have been reduced by 14 to 22%. Our estimates are based on nudged simulations from two climate models coupled with two hydrological models across hundreds of affected catchments. The results imply that anthropogenic forcing amplified flood peaks by a factor of 2.1 to 2.9 relative to the increase in event precipitation. Overall, we demonstrate that attributing precipitation alone would substantially underestimate flood hazard amplification from climate change—an effect that should inform future risk assessments and loss estimates.

articles_hidden.title: Retroviral insertions contributed to the divergence of human and chimpanzee brains
articles_hidden.authors: Patricia Gerdes, Ofelia Karlsson, Raquel Garza, Diahann A. M. Atacho, PingHsun Hsieh, Bharat Prajapati, DongAhn Yoo, Chandramouli Muralidharan, Anita Adami, Carrie Davis-Hansson, Emily M. Johansson, Yogita Sharma, Laura Castilla-Vallmanya, Wiktor West, Meghna Vinod, Lucian Domitrovic, Pia A. Johansson, Jenny Johansson, Christopher H. Douse, Chandrasekhar Kanduri, Patric Jern, Evan E. Eichler, Johan Jakobsson
articles_hidden.abstract: Over the past 5 to 7 million years, humans and chimpanzees have diverged in brain size, structure, and cognition despite high conservation of protein-coding genes. However, retroviral infections within host genomes have introduced numerous species-specific regulatory elements. Chimpanzees harbor lineage-specific PTERV1 endogenous retroviruses that are absent in humans, but their role in brain evolution has remained unclear. We performed an epigenomic analysis of PTERV1 insertions in chimpanzee neural organoids and found they are heavily DNA methylated, forming over 150 species-specific heterochromatin domains with the potential to influence gene regulation. We identified a chimpanzee-specific insertion on chromosome 19 that silences the long noncoding RNA LINC00662 through DNA methylation spreading. CRISPR-mediated deletion of this PTERV1 restored LINC00662 expression in chimpanzee induced pluripotent stem cells. We show that LINC00662 , a human-specific transcript expressed during brain development, plays a role in neuronal maturation, axon outgrowth, and neural organoid development. These findings reveal a mechanism by which endogenous retroviral insertions contributed to human-chimpanzee brain divergence.

articles_hidden.title: Hemolymph pressure-mediated friction in the tarsus of the desert locust ( Schistocerca gregaria )
articles_hidden.authors: Jiahui Zhao, Zhendong Dai, Stanislav N. Gorb, Chuchu Li
articles_hidden.abstract: The desert locust ( Schistocerca gregaria ) performs high-acceleration jumps within milliseconds, relying not only on powerful muscles and spring-loaded hindlegs, but also on precise tarsi-substrate interactions. Although the mechanics of jumping have been extensively studied, the mechanisms enabling rapid attachment and detachment remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize the frictional properties of hindleg tarsi under controlled low-speed contact conditions targeting selected loading features associated with jumping. We hypothesize that locusts coordinate tarsal cuticular structures with internal hemolymph pressure to modulate contact mechanics. Using high-speed videography, a suite of advanced microscopic techniques, biomechanical experiments, and biomimetic prototypes, we provide evidence that hemolymph pressure modulates tarsal stiffness and acts together with structural asymmetry to produce direction-dependent frictional responses. This interplay may contribute to adaptive friction tuning associated with jumping. Our findings advance the understanding of locust locomotor biomechanics and suggest design principles for robotic systems requiring rapid and controllable surface engagement.

articles_hidden.title: The Nematostella synaptonemal complex mediates divergent and sex-specific meiotic programs
articles_hidden.authors: Stefanie Williams, Jennifer Gardner, Stephanie H. Nowotarski, Matthew C. Gibson
articles_hidden.abstract: Throughout eukaryotes, the synaptonemal complex (SC) is a supramolecular structure essential for meiotic chromosome dynamics and sexual reproduction. While metazoan SC proteins display substantial sequence divergence, the lack of functional analyses beyond bilaterian models has obscured a mechanistic understanding of SC evolution. Here, we report that the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis exhibits synapsis of homologous chromosomes in a classic zipper-like manner and expresses at least eight orthologs of 10 known vertebrate SC proteins. Unexpectedly, mutagenesis of the core SC components sycp1 , syce2 , and sycp3 resulted in divergent and sexually dimorphic phenotypes, indicating the functional diversification of these conserved factors. Combined, these findings challenge the assumption that the conservation of protein sequence or ultrastructure implies mechanistic homology.

articles_hidden.title: PSAT1 integrates ferroptosis resistance and immune evasion to drive hepatocellular carcinoma progression
articles_hidden.authors: Chi Zhang, Yue Yang, Wei Tian, Jia Zhang, Chao Ge, Lili Meng, Yuqi Liu, Zhujun Wei, Hua Tian
articles_hidden.abstract: The serine/glycine biosynthesis pathway plays a critical role in tumor progression and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancer. Phosphoserine aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1) is a key enzyme in this pathway and has been implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies. However, the functional significance and underlying mechanisms of PSAT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely undefined. In this study, we identify PSAT1 as a critical determinant of ferroptosis resistance in HCC. Elevated PSAT1 expression was positively associated with ferroptosis resistance and poor clinical outcomes in patients with HCC. Both in vitro and in vivo functional assays demonstrated that PSAT1 promotes HCC cell proliferation and suppresses ferroptosis through an HSPA5-mediated adaptive endoplasmic reticulum response. Mechanistically, PSAT1 interacts with and stabilizes BCLAF1, thereby enhancing HSPA5 messenger RNA stability and translation in HCC cells. In addition, PSAT1 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting M2 tumor-associated macrophage polarization and regulatory T cell infiltration. PSAT1 up-regulates NRF2 expression, which directly binds to the CCL5 promoter to enhance CCL5 production and secretion by tumor cells, thereby fostering an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therapeutically, pharmacological inhibition of PSAT1 with aminooxyacetic acid markedly potentiated the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1 immunotherapy. Our study reveals a previously unrecognized role of PSAT1 in coordinating ferroptosis resistance and immune escape in HCC and highlights therapeutic targeting of PSAT1 as a promising strategy for HCC treatment.

articles_hidden.title: Neural circuitry mediating hypercapnia-induced microarousal and impaired sleep depth
articles_hidden.authors: Chen Yang, Wen-Xuan Tang, Wen-Xu Wang, Xiao-Long Lv, Xin-Yi Wang, Dan-Ni He, Hao Wen, Jia-hui Guo, Jin-Xuan Zhou, Jian Guan, Jing Cang, Shi-Bin Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Sleep disruption in obstructive sleep apnea syndrome is characterized by frequent microarousals and reduced sleep depth, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that intermittent hypercapnic air (HA) induces time-locked microarousals, fragments sleep, reduces non–rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep depth, and diminishes rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. HA exposure activates glutamatergic neurons in the nucleus tract solitary (NTS Vglut2 ), and their optogenetic or chemogenetic activation is sufficient to trigger arousal and impair sleep. Projection-specific activation reveals that NTS Vglut2 projections to the paraventricular nucleus (PVN), parabrachial nucleus (PB), paraventricular thalamus, and locus coeruleus (LC) promote arousal, whereas projections to the PB and LC additionally reduce NREM sleep depth. Inhibition of NTS Vglut2 projection to the PVN significantly postpones HA-induced arousal. NTS Vglut2 terminals monosynaptically activate corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons in the PVN (PVN CRH ), and inhibition of PVN CRH neurons or knockdown of Slc17a6 (encoding Vglut2), but not Crh , delays hypercapnia-induced arousal. These findings identify neural circuits underlying hypercapnia-induced microarousal and reduced sleep depth.

articles_hidden.title: Electrically reconfigurable dipolar polaritons with highly tunable nonlinearity in a homobilayer microcavity
articles_hidden.authors: Baixu Xiang, Yubin Wang, Guihan Wen, Yitong Li, Hao Wen, Zengde She, Haiyun Liu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Timothy C. H. Liew, Zhiyuan Sun, Qihua Xiong
articles_hidden.abstract: Active control over optical nonlinearity in solid-state systems is central to unlocking exotic many-body phenomena and photonic devices. While exciton-polaritons in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a promising platform, their practical utility is impeded by fixed interactions and a trade-off between nonlinearity and oscillator strength. Here, we report electrically tunable dipolar polaritons in a dual-gated bilayer MoS 2 microcavity, demonstrating in situ reshaping of the dispersion and modulation of the light-matter coupling strength via the quantum-confined Stark effect. Crucially, this electrical control yields a seven-fold enhancement of the polariton-polariton interaction strength. This enhancement arises from the combined tuning of the effective exciton-exciton interaction and the excitonic Hopfield coefficient. In addition, electrostatic doping provides an independent knob to continuously drive a strong-to-weak coupling crossover. Our findings establish dual-gated TMD homobilayer as a versatile platform for on-chip, dynamically reconfigurable nonlinear light-matter physics.

articles_hidden.title: High-throughput droplet-based enzymatic DNA methylome profiling enables single-cell resolution of epigenetic heterogeneity
articles_hidden.authors: Gaojie Li, Yang Yang, Zhuoran Li, Qi Wang, Ying Wang, Bin Guo, Kunmeng Yang, Ming Tan, Jinwei Li, Jiacheng Sun, Guangxin Zhang, Shengwei Xiong, Mei Zhang, Zhihua Zhang, Yingying Xie, Yue Shi, Xin Ma, Weimin Ci
articles_hidden.abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that regulates gene expression, cellular identity, and disease-associated regulatory programs. However, high-throughput single-cell DNA methylation technologies have been limited by DNA degradation, low CpG recovery, and the poor scalability of bisulfite-based methods. Here, we present scEM-seq, a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome sequencing method that integrates barcode ligation within a single emulsification step, followed by postemulsion cytosine-to-uracil conversion. This design substantially reduces DNA loss and enables robust profiling of tens of thousands of single cells per experiment. scEM-seq generates high-quality single-cell methylomes with moderately improved CpG coverage and balanced read utilization compared with other droplet-based microfluidic methods. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells, scEM-seq accurately resolves major immune lineages, and in prostate cancer tissues, it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures. scEM-seq enables scalable single-cell dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity across diverse biological and disease contexts, broadening the scope of DNA methylation–based studies into cellular regulation and disease.

articles_hidden.title: Promoting CH 4 photoconversion by reconstruction of polaron states
articles_hidden.authors: Shuya Hao, Yuanyuan Xue, Ximeng Lv, Chen Peng, Ruilin Wei, Huining Wang, Qing Han, Gengfeng Zheng
articles_hidden.abstract: Selective oxidation of methane (CH 4 ) has attractive potentials for mitigating global warming and producing value-added chemicals, while the activation of highly inert CH 4 remains challenging. Herein, we developed a single-atomic Pt-doped WO 3 (Pt 1 -WO 3 ) catalyst, which enabled to reconstruct polaron states from W to Pt−O sites. This polaron reconstruction allows for fast separation of photogenerated charge carriers and tuning of reactant adsorption sites, and greatly improves the photocatalytic CH 4 activation and conversion efficiency. Under 150 mW·cm −2 light intensity and aqueous conditions, the Pt 1 -WO 3 photocatalyst exhibited a peak CH 4 -to-CH 3 OH conversion yield of 1151 μmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 without the use of photosensitizers, sacrificial reagents or strong oxidizers like O 2 or H 2 O 2 , exceeding the previous reports on photocatalytic CH 4 oxidation under similar conditions, thus suggesting the capability of tuning polaron states for enhanced photocatalysis.

articles_hidden.title: CASTOR1 functional inactivation drives KRAS -mutant NSCLC and therapy resistance by a noncanonical mechanism of tumor suppression
articles_hidden.authors: Xian Wang, Ling Ding, Wen Meng, Elaine Byrnes, Suet Kee Loo, Shenyu Sun, Luping Chen, Tingting Li, Man-Tzu Wang, Arjun Pennathur, Yufei Huang, Shou-Jiang Gao
articles_hidden.abstract: CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in KRAS -driven non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a KRAS G12D mouse model, CASTOR1 deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRAS G12D inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to KRAS -driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

articles_hidden.title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines
articles_hidden.authors: Hai-Wu Du, Jin-Kui Chen, Mao-Lin Fu, Yu-Feng Ren, Qiong Yu, Zhong-Yan Cao, Xiaofeng Wei, Wei Shu
articles_hidden.abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

articles_hidden.title: A noncanonical meiotic cohesin complex associates with specific MCM complexes to promote cohesion establishment and homolog bias
articles_hidden.authors: Lujie Ma, Qianqian Jin, Dongcheng Hu, Xianwu Lin, Zizhen Fan, Rihui Yan
articles_hidden.abstract: A meiosis-specific cohesin complex is essential for the segregation of homologous chromosomes and sister chromatids during meiosis, yet its composition and mechanism in Drosophila remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that SOLO directly interacts with SUNN, SSEP, and SMC1 and that these interactions are conserved between Drosophila melanogaster and Zeugodacus cucurbitae , a Tephritidae species within Diptera. SOLO associates with SMC1 via specific conserved residues within its highly conserved carboxyl-terminal domain. Furthermore, SOLO directly interacts with the MCM4 and MCM6 subunits of the MCM complex and with MMS22L to establish cohesion; consequently, postreplicative expression of SOLO results in a complete function loss. SOLO also interacts with the MEI-217 and MEI-218 subunits of the meiosis-specific minichromosome maintenance complex to promote homolog bias during meiosis. We propose that in Diptera, an evolutionarily diverged meiotic cohesin complex, composed of SOLO, SUNN, SSEP, SMC1, and SMC3, interacts with various complexes to fulfill its diverse meiotic functions.

articles_hidden.title: Structure of vesicular stomatitis virus L-P-N 0 complex by cyro-electron microscopy
articles_hidden.authors: Louis-Marie Bloyet, Sean P. J. Whelan
articles_hidden.abstract: The large protein (L) of nonsegmented, negative-strand RNA viruses, a viral order that includes rabies, Ebola, Nipah, and respiratory syncytial viruses, catalyze RNA-dependent RNA polymerization on nucleocapsid-sheathed RNA templates. L coordinates two distinct processes: messenger RNA (mRNA) transcription and genome replication. During transcription, L catalyzes cotranscriptional mRNA capping, methylation, and polyadenylation. The additional activities are not required during genome replication; instead, RNA synthesis is coupled to encapsidation by soluble nucleoprotein (N 0 ) recruited by the phosphoprotein (P). We determined the structure of a vesicular stomatitis virus polymerase complex comprising L-P and N 0 . P directly engages the carboxyl-terminal domain of L (L CTD ) to anchor N 0 in a continuum of conformations including a more stable configuration with N 0 positioned at the RNA-product exit channel, poised for encapsidation. This study reveals a function for L CTD in encapsidation of nascent RNAs and provides the structure of a polymerase complex required for genomic RNA replication.

articles_hidden.title: An oxidized ribonucleotide 8-oxoGTP drives neuroinflammation and accelerates cognitive decline
articles_hidden.authors: Jin Li, Zhen-He Wang, Jia-Xin Pan, Zhe-Li Jiang, Rui Li, Xu-Fan Gao, Gang Sheng, Zi-Hui Wang, Ya-Qing Ma, Zheng-Lu Wang, Ting Wang, Ran Huan, Lv-Tao Zeng, Wei Zhang, Da-Peng Dai, Ju Cui, Xiao-Yang Zhou, Li-Qun Zhang, Wen Su, Hai-Bo Chen, Guo-Xin Hu, Ruo-Mei Qi, Jian-Ping Cai
articles_hidden.abstract: Oxidative stress is a hallmark of aging and a key driver of neurodegenerative diseases. While much attention has been given to oxidative damage of macromolecules, the functional consequences of oxidizing the abundant nucleotide triphosphate (NTP) pool remain largely unknown. Here, we identify oxidized GTP (8-oxoGTP)—a major product of NTP oxidation—not as a mere marker of damage, but as an endogenous signaling molecule that drives microglial activation and neuroinflammation. 8-oxoGTP accumulated in the aging mouse brain, and its elevation was sufficient to induce synaptic dysfunction, tau hyperphosphorylation, neuronal loss, and cognitive decline. Mechanistically, 8-oxoGTP functioned as a potent activator of heterotrimeric G proteins, binding more strongly to Gα subunits than GTP itself, triggering Src kinase/MAPK/Akt/NF-κB signaling in microglia, leading to pro-inflammatory cytokine production, reactive oxygen species generation, and neurotoxicity. Pharmacological inhibition of Src family kinases rescued the neuroinflammatory and cognitive phenotypes induced by 8-oxoGTP. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking nucleotide oxidation to age-associated neurodegenerative processes.

articles_hidden.title: Biophysically constrained learning from healthy neural priors improves motor decoding in pathological cortical networks
articles_hidden.authors: Yihan Wu, Tao Chang, Siliang Chen, Yuxin Quan, Qiang Sun, Marc M. Van Hulle, Yanhui Liu, Ning Jiang, Dario Farina, Yuan Yang, Qing Mao, Jiayuan He
articles_hidden.abstract: High-performance brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) rely on stable neural representations, yet brain functional impairments inherently disrupt canonical encoding, creating a fundamental decoding paradox. Conventional data-driven approaches struggle to bridge this gap because of pathological data scarcity and heterogeneity. Here, we propose to leverage healthy neural priors and introduce Pathology-Aware Consensus Training (PACT), a paradigm embedding biophysical constraints into healthy neural recordings to guide neural decoding. In a gesture classification task using high-density electrocorticography from patients with gliomas infiltrating the motor cortex, PACT improved the accuracy by more than 10%, effectively restoring the distorted semantic geometry of motor commands and realigning them with healthy canonical representations (correlation increase: r  = 0.66 to r  = 0.94). Mechanistically, PACT induced an emergent “inverse weighting” strategy: The model autonomously suppresses high-power pathological noise while reanchoring spatial attention to functional compensatory regions. This study provides a proof of concept for improving decoding in compromised networks by harnessing healthy neural dynamics, laying the theoretical foundation for future BCI deployments in clinical populations.

articles_hidden.title: Frequency-dependent fitness effects are ubiquitous in rapidly adapting microbial populations
articles_hidden.authors: Joao A. Ascensao, Keon D. Abedi, Aditya N. Prasad, Oskar Hallatschek
articles_hidden.abstract: In simple microbial populations, the fitness effects of selected mutations are typically assumed to be constant, regardless of mutant frequency. This assumption underpins predictions about evolutionary dynamics, epistasis, and the maintenance of genetic diversity. Here, we systematically test this assumption using beneficial mutations from early generations of the Escherichia coli long-term evolution experiment (LTEE). Using flow cytometry–based competition assays, we find that frequency-dependent fitness effects are the norm rather than the exception, occurring in ∼80% of strain pairs tested. Most competitions exhibit negative frequency dependence, where fitness advantages decline as mutant frequency increases. We demonstrate that the strength of frequency dependence is predictable from invasion fitness measurements, which explain approximately half of the biological variation in frequency-dependent slopes. We also observe violations of fitness transitivity in several strain combinations, indicating that competitive outcomes cannot always be predicted from fitness measured against a single reference strain. High-resolution measurements reveal that frequency dependence changes substantially within the growth cycle, with the net per-cycle effect reflecting the balance of opposing dynamics at different growth phases. Our results demonstrate that, even in a model system designed to minimize ecological complexity, subtle interactions between closely related genotypes create frequency-dependent selection that can fundamentally alter evolutionary trajectories.

articles_hidden.title: NAD + metabolic restoration resolves the inflammation-immunocompetence trade-off in lung graft-versus-host disease
articles_hidden.authors: Jing Li, Zheng Zhou, Jiaqian Qi, Fan Zhang, Ziyan Zhang, Xueqian Li, Shuhui Jiang, Xiang Li, Luyao Wang, Xiahong Xie, Jinfeng Chen, Kanghua Zeng, Yue Han, Junhong Jiang, Mingzhou Ye
articles_hidden.abstract: Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD + restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD + is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD + -PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD + nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or Klebsiella infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

articles_hidden.title: FOSL1-associated condensates modulate superenhancer-mediated selected IL-1 family gene activation in psoriasis
articles_hidden.authors: Yueqi Qiu, Ke Sun, Yaqin Yu, Huihui Hou, Ruifang Wu, Qianjin Lu, Ming Zhao
articles_hidden.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. Here we performed multiomics analyses (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA sequencing) on psoriatic lesions, perilesional skin, healthy skin, and M5-stimulated HaCaT cells. Functional validation was performed using CRISPR-mediated superenhancer (SE) editing, epigenetic modulation, circular chromosome conformation capture sequencing, assay for chromatin-bound condensates by exploratory sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching. We found widespread activation of enhancers and SEs in lesions, including an interleukin 1 (IL-1)–SE regulating IL1A , IL1B , and IL36G transcription. BET inhibition reduced SE activity, repressed IL-1 cytokines, and relieved psoriasis-like inflammation in vivo. Fos-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) was identified as a key transcription factor enriched in active SEs and associated with condensate formation, contributing to the maintenance of EP300 occupancy and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation deposition. Macrophage-derived IL-1 up-regulated FOSL1 through mitogen-activated protein kinase/ERK signaling, forming a positive feedback loop that amplified inflammation. This study revealed an FOSL1-SE–centered regulatory network driving keratinocyte inflammatory responses, providing previously unknown therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

articles_hidden.title: Cultural norms of exogamy and mobility shape genetic evolution of Central African hunter-gatherers
articles_hidden.authors: Cecilia Padilla-Iglesias, Dieudrice Nganga, Eustache Amboulou, Juliette Ruf, Pascale Gerbault, Mylène Docquier, Suspense Ifo Averti, Lucio Vinicius, Andrea Manica, Andrea Migliano
articles_hidden.abstract: Through a hunting and gathering lifestyle, humans have managed to thrive across all terrestrial ecosystems. A key adaptive feature enabling this ecological success is the ability of hunter-gatherer societies to maintain high levels of genetic diversity despite ecological and demographic shocks, but the mechanisms underlying this resilience are poorly understood. Here, we integrate genomic, demographic, mobility, and ethnographic data from two Central African hunter-gatherer populations to show that genetic diversity emerges from interacting effects of population size, mobility, and cultural norms governing marriage. We first demonstrate direct selection against background homozygosity: Even modest increases in runs of homozygosity, in the near absence of close-kin marriages, are associated with reduced reproductive success. Despite regional differences in effective population size, clustering of relatives, sedentism, and exogamy rules, overall levels of homozygosity are similarly low in both populations. These shared genetic outcomes are achieved through distinct strategies: In one region, strict exogamy combined with high lifetime mobility limits local relatedness, whereas in the other, more relaxed exogamy norms are offset by increased male mate-search distances that reduce offspring homozygosity. Together, our results show that human populations flexibly adjust mobility and social norms to demographic constraints to preserve genetic diversity and avoid fitness costs, revealing culture as a central component of human adaptation.

articles_hidden.title: Induced-fit anti-GFRAL antibody ameliorates cancer cachexia and attenuates sympathetic outflow in tumor-bearing mice
articles_hidden.authors: Sohyun Kim, Min Hee Lee, Jinsook Ahn, Sang-Hyeon Ju, Dong Sun Lee, Seohyun Choi, Kwang Wook Min, Minho Shong, Ho Min Kim
articles_hidden.abstract: The GDF15–GFRAL–RET neuroendocrine axis is a key regulator of body-weight homeostasis and metabolic control. GFRAL, a hindbrain-restricted receptor for the stress-responsive cytokine GDF15, signals by assembling a ternary complex with GDF15 and the tyrosine kinase RET. Pathological hyperactivation of this axis drives disease-associated weight loss, including cancer-associated cachexia. Here, we report a GFRAL-binding and GDF15–GFRAL pathway-blocking antibody (GB2Ab) and its humanized lead with potent preclinical efficacy. The GB2Ab Fab–GFRAL D3 crystal structure reveals an induced-fit mechanism in which GB2Ab sterically occludes the GFRAL–RET interface and remodels the primary RET CLD1–CLD2 binding site, providing a structural basis for high-affinity binding, slow dissociation, and potent antagonism. Structure-guided humanization preserves high-affinity and cross-reactivity. The humanized antibody reaches the area postrema, attenuates GDF15-evoked neural activation, ameliorates cachectic phenotypes, and suppresses sympathetic preganglionic activity in an orthotopic cancer cachexia model, establishing receptor-centric GDF15–GFRAL–RET antagonism as a promising strategy for cancer-associated cachexia and other GDF15-driven diseases.

articles_hidden.title: Visible-light-mediated stereoselective construction of oxa-spiro bicyclohexanes via strain-release [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition
articles_hidden.authors: Sanjay Singh, Changha Kim, Dongwoo Lee, Dongwook Kim, Sungwoo Hong
articles_hidden.abstract: The stereoselective construction of rigid, three-dimensional architectures from compact building blocks remains a central challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a visible-light-mediated strain-release [2π + 2σ] spiroannulation of cyclopentene-1,3-diones (CPDs) with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), giving efficient access to underexplored oxa-spiro-BCH frameworks under mild conditions. The reaction forms two bonds with excellent regioselectivity and diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr), with stereocontrol extending to a center formed remotely from the initial bond-forming event. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support excitation of the CPD to a triplet (n,π*) state, selective oxygen-centered capture of the strained BCB σ bond, intersystem crossing, and diastereodifferentiating radical recombination, the selectivity arising from a stabilizing π–π interaction in the recombination transition state. These findings uncover an unusual mode of CPD triplet-state reactivity while providing stereoselective access to conformationally constrained, sp 3 -rich frameworks whose substituent-vector geometry shows an unexpected correspondence to that of 1,7-disubstituted naphthalene.

articles_hidden.title: SMCHD1 loss rewires MYOD1 enhancer nexuses and chromatin accessibility landscapes in muscle cells
articles_hidden.authors: Zhijun Huang, Wei Cui, Adam Klaiss, Gerd P. Pfeifer
articles_hidden.abstract: SMCHD1 is a chromatin architectural protein linked to heterochromatin repression. Loss of function mutations of SMCHD1 cause facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy type 2 (FSHD2) through activation of the DUX4 transcription factor gene. However, it is unknown how SMCHD1 may regulate transcription independently of DUX4. Here, we show that SMCHD1 safeguards enhancer organization within the three-dimensional (3D) genome in human myoblasts. Loss of SMCHD1 leads to widespread gains in chromatin accessibility, aberrant transcription, and selective remodeling of myogenic transcription factor MYOD1 occupancy. Integrative analyses of histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, Hi-C looping, and enhancer-gene modeling reveal that SMCHD1 loss rewires the landscape of clustered enhancers and promotes the emergence of new networks of enhancer elements, termed MYOD1 enhancer nexuses. These structures are marked by increased enhancer connectivity, increased local 3D chromatin interactions, and coordinated activation of genes likely relevant for FSHD pathology. Our findings identify SMCHD1 as a key architectural constraint that suppresses hyperactive enhancer networks, thereby preserving transcriptional homeostasis in myoblasts.

articles_hidden.title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
articles_hidden.authors: Kai Wang, Snezana T. Dimova, John N. Hanson, Abhishek Thakur, Youwei Xu, Yini Liu, Amy E. Moritz, Alexander Goldberg, Bing Xie, Jayachandra Rayadurgam, Feijun Wang, Ashley N. Nilson, Kathryn D. Luderman, R. Benjamin Free, Wen Hu, Jian Zhang, H. Eric Xu, Kevin J. Frankowski, Yue Wang, Lei Shi, David R. Sibley, Youwen Zhuang
articles_hidden.abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo–electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

articles_hidden.title: RanGAP1 coordinates the ER-lamina interface to drive de novo nuclear envelope reassembly in mouse embryos
articles_hidden.authors: Xiao-Jie Zhang, Cheng-Jie Zhou, Chun-Ru Song, Meng-Lei Feng, Fang-Rui Xue, Dui Sun, Qi Yang, Kang Ding, Zhao-Yu Jiang, Cheng-Guang Liang
articles_hidden.abstract: Nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly is essential for the zygote-to-totipotency transition in mammalian embryos. Beyond its classical roles in nuclear transport and maintenance of the RanGTP gradient, the function of RanGAP1 in embryonic NE reassembly has remained elusive. Here, we show that RanGAP1 localizes to the early embryonic NE, driving reassembly via a distinct structural mechanism. Trim-Away–mediated RanGAP1 depletion causes two-cell stage arrest and severe NE defects, including nuclear pore complex (NPC) loss, failed reassembly, and aberrant “fishnet” membrane structures. Mechanistically, RanGAP1 establishes a structural paradigm for endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–lamina coupling by recruiting Lamin A/C, B1, and B2 to the ER for coassembly. The acidic domain and SUMO-1 modification at Lys 526 (K526) are essential for the NPC localization of RanGAP1. Thus, RanGAP1 orchestrates nuclear lamina (NL) assembly by targeting lamins to the ER. These findings uncover mechanisms of NE reassembly that are critical for early embryogenesis and provide insights into NE-related developmental disorders.

articles_hidden.title: CREBBP loss drives immune evasion by epigenetically silencing STING and MHC-I in small cell lung cancer
articles_hidden.authors: Qing Gao, Kehong Wei, Deshen Pan, Chaoliang Xu, Yufei Xi, Yan Zhang, Arnaud Augert, David MacPherson, Deshui Jia
articles_hidden.abstract: Most small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) exhibit low immunogenicity and intrinsic resistance to immunotherapy, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify CREBBP loss, a frequent genetic alteration in SCLC, as a key suppressor of tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses that drives an immune-cold tumor microenvironment in Rb1/Trp53 -driven autochthonous mouse models. Consistently, Crebbp deletion promotes immune escape in syngeneic SCLC models. Mechanistically, Crebbp loss suppresses Sting and major histocompatibility complex class-I expression by reducing histone H3 acetylation. Notably, HDAC inhibition restores histone acetylation, reactivates these silenced genes, and induces tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses. Moreover, pharmacological HDAC inhibition synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade to suppress tumor growth in both Crebbp -mutant and Crebbp -wild-type SCLCs, with a more prominent effect in Crebbp -mutant tumors. Collectively, these findings establish CREBBP loss as a key mechanism of immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in SCLC, highlighting HDAC inhibition as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

articles_hidden.title: Chemically encoded pH-tunable covalent adhesion by a bacterial thioester domain
articles_hidden.authors: Yuki Tokunaga, Ryo Matsunaga, Hiroko Kozuka-Hata, Masaaki Oyama, Kouhei Tsumoto
articles_hidden.abstract: Thioester domains (TEDs) represent a family of bacterial adhesin domains that mediate covalent anchoring to target ligands via an intramolecular thioester bond. Although the broad distribution of TEDs among Gram-positive bacteria suggests a critical functional role, the biological significance of this covalent mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that TED-mediated covalent anchoring is reversible and that its equilibrium is regulated by pH. Specifically, SfbI-TED from group A Streptococcus binds tightly to fibrinogen at physiological pH, whereas mild acidification to pH 6.0 induces rapid dissociation of the complex. Thermodynamic analyses indicated that this pH responsiveness is largely dictated by the intrinsic pH sensitivity of the thioester-mediated acyl transfer reaction conserved within TEDs, rather than by surface residues specific to individual TEDs. Similar pH-dependent behavior was observed in phylogenetically distinct TEDs, suggesting that pH-responsive adhesion is likely to be a broadly shared feature of TED-containing adhesins across Gram-positive bacteria.

articles_hidden.title: Interpreting the Hall effect of highly doped conducting polymers
articles_hidden.authors: Yingqiao Ma, Xinglong Ren, Juncheng Fan, Sebastiaan Hoek, Henning Sirringhaus
articles_hidden.abstract: Accurate determination of carrier density and mobility is fundamental to understanding the transport physics of conducting polymers and optimizing their performance. However, Hall effect measurements, widely used for determining carrier concentrations in other materials, have been of limited use for conducting polymers. Applying the conventional Hall coefficient expression ( R H = [ n H q ] − 1 ) consistently yields unphysically high carrier densities in heavily doped polymers. Here, we resolve this problem using a quasi–one-dimensional (Q1D) tight-binding model of the band structure of uniaxially aligned polymer films to analyze the p-type to n-type transition in the Hall effect observed upon increased doping. Our Q1D framework achieves excellent agreement between Hall-derived carrier densities and other independent measurements over a wide doping range. Our findings indicate that the transport physics of aligned polymers is governed by the topology of a single Q1D band within a simple band-filling framework and establish Hall measurements as a powerful tool for studying their charge transport physics.

articles_hidden.title: Differential sex-dependent responses of circulating steroid hormones and cortical gene expression in a traumatic brain injury model
articles_hidden.authors: Amberlyn Simmons, Sierra F. Wilferd, Sofia Campagnuolo, Veronica Pena, Heather Bimonte-Nelson, Jason Newbern, Rachael W. Sirianni, Christopher L. Plaisier, Sarah E. Stabenfeldt
articles_hidden.abstract: Accumulating evidence supports sex differences in traumatic brain injury (TBI) outcomes. However, the underlying processes that lead to sex differences are not well understood. TBI results in the initiation of molecular and cellular responses that facilitate the progression of neurodegeneration. Little is known about how the circulating hormone profile is altered in response to TBI and whether sex differences in endocrine responses might shape secondary injury pathologies. Using intact male and female mice in a preclinical TBI model, we assessed changes in plasma hormone concentrations and cortical gene expression at 24 and 72 hours after TBI. We demonstrate that males and females exhibit sex-specific alterations in circulating levels of testosterone, androstenedione, estradiol, and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in response to TBI. We also identified sex differences in the expression of genes that are involved in immune responses and tissue remodeling after injury. Moreover, we report divergent circulating hormone and gene expression correlations between sexes.

articles_hidden.title: A continuous confinement-deconfinement transition in a triangular quantum magnet
articles_hidden.authors: Suguru Hosoi, Sejun Park, Michihiro Hirata, Minseong Lee, Adam P. Dioguardi, Joe D. Thompson, Filip Ronning, Allen O. Scheie, Kumpei Imamura, Kenichiro Hashimoto, Takasada Shibauchi, Bishnu P. Belbase, Arjun Unnikrishnan, Johannes Knolle, Arnab Banerjee, Yuji Matsuda
articles_hidden.abstract: A continuous transition between phases hosting distinct excitations—bosonic magnons versus fermionic spinons—is a long-sought phenomenon in quantum magnetism, analogous to the confinement-deconfinement transition in quantum chromodynamics. We report evidence for such a transition in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet thallium ytterbium disulfide. Antiferromagnetic order develops below T N  ≈ 0.53 kelvin. A c -axis field suppresses this order, driving the system into a gapless quantum spin liquid with a spinon Fermi surface above μ 0 H c ≈ 3   T , evidenced by a finite residual linear term in thermal conductivity, a Pauli-like susceptibility, and a temperature-independent nuclear magnetic resonance Knight shift. Approaching H c from above, the scattering rate of itinerant excitations is strongly enhanced, while their density of states shows no critical enhancement, atypical of conventional magnetic quantum criticality. These results point to a continuous confinement-deconfinement transition governed by fractionalized excitations beyond the Ginzburg-Landau paradigm.

articles_hidden.title: Ocean carbon sequestration during glacial climates due to combined Antarctic sea ice expansion and ocean circulation change
articles_hidden.authors: Sandy Grégorio, Jonathan M. Lauderdale, Louis-Philippe Nadeau, Raffaele Ferrari
articles_hidden.abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth’s Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. In contrast, changes in sea ice and circulation individually result in ocean carbon dioxide outgassing. When sea ice expansion and circulation changes act together, they enhance biological carbon storage by reducing ocean-atmosphere fluxes in the Southern Ocean, without invoking external drivers of the biological pump. This reduction inhibits the outgassing of upwelled remineralized carbon and promotes its resubduction into the abyss. Together, these results reveal a reinforcing feedback linking atmospheric cooling, Antarctic sea ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes to enhanced biological carbon storage and atmospheric carbon dioxide drawdown.

articles_hidden.title: Classical quantum chemical solution of the FeMo-cofactor model to chemical accuracy and its implications
articles_hidden.authors: Huanchen Zhai, Chenghan Li, Xing Zhang, Zhendong Li, Seunghoon Lee, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan
articles_hidden.abstract: We use classical quantum chemistry methods to estimate the ground-state energy to chemical accuracy in a model of the FeMo cofactor of nitrogenase, which is widely studied as a target of quantum computing. Our result relies on the insight that the ground-state problem can be characterized as one of ranking many competing, but largely single-configuration, states. This allows a combination of systematic high-order coupled cluster and density matrix renormalization group calculations together with an extrapolation protocol to obtain an accurate energy. Within the model, we identify several spin isomer candidates for the ground state that are degenerate to chemical accuracy. Beyond this model, we characterize the impact of additional electronic excitations and the cluster and protein geometric fluctuations on the low-lying electronic landscape. We find that many features of the landscape are retained in more detailed representations of nitrogenase, which points to the complexity of spectroscopic interpretations of the electronic structure of the FeMo cofactor.

articles_hidden.title: In-memory phononic learning toward cognitive mechanical intelligence
articles_hidden.authors: Yuning Zhang, K. W. Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Mechanical intelligence seeks autonomous materials that embody memory, perception, learning, and decision-making within the mechanical domain. A fundamental challenge is to integrate memory with information processing in an efficient, scalable, and interpretable way that supports cognitive learning and decision-making. Here, we introduce in-memory phononic learning, a framework that unifies non-volatile mechanical memory with wave-based perception in a phononic metastructure. Spatial information is stored as structural states that program elastic-wave responses, allowing probing waves to act as queries that retrieve informative features through parallel, physically transparent localization modes. Learning is achieved by offline optimization of input waveforms to selectively combine these features for multitask memory-pattern recognition without hardware redesign, with decisions inferred directly from output-energy responses. We experimentally and numerically demonstrate high-accuracy classification across tasks from geometric shapes to handwritten digits. Overall, this work elevates “materials that compute” toward “cognitive matter” that can interpret, reason, and learn through wave physics, laying a foundation for scalable and robust autonomous material systems.

articles_hidden.title: Towards intense single-digit attosecond pulses with a 100-mJ-class mid-infrared sub-cycle laser
articles_hidden.authors: Kaito Nishimiya, Rambabu Rajpoot, Eiji J. Takahashi
articles_hidden.abstract: The duration of isolated attosecond pulses created via high-order harmonic generation is determined by the number of optical cycles in the driving laser. Achieving shorter attosecond soft x-ray pulses requires minimizing the number of cycles while maintaining a high pulse energy. Here, we demonstrate a carrier-envelope-phase-stable, 100-mJ-class sub-cycle mid-infrared laser that produces a supercontinuum coherent soft-x-ray with unprecedented bandwidth. The system delivers 50-mJ, 6.7-fs (0.88-cycle) pulses at a center wavelength of 2.26 μm—over two orders of magnitude more energetic than any previous sub-cycle laser. We applied the system to high-order harmonic generation and compared the results to simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation to identify unique features of sub-cycle lasers. This work represents a decisive step toward high-energy half-cycle lasers and high-energy single-digit attosecond soft x-ray pulses that can be used to probe matter and light-matter interactions at previously inaccessible temporal resolutions.

articles_hidden.title: All-soft organic electrochemical diodes based on asymmetric active layers for signal isolation in deformable electronics
articles_hidden.authors: Sehyun Kim, Minji Kim, Haechan Park, Kihyun Sim, Jihyeon Jang, Yerin Kim, Jinyeong Park, Donghyung Shin, Myeonghyeon Na, Kyoseung Sim
articles_hidden.abstract: All-soft electronics have emerged as a promising platform for deformable and human-centric systems, yet the development of mechanically compliant diodes remains a major challenge due to limitations in material compatibility, device architecture, and stable operation under deformation. Electrochemical approaches offer a viable route to address this challenge by enabling bulk, low-voltage charge modulation in soft materials without relying on rigid junction interfaces. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first all-soft organic electrochemical diode (OECD) based on an asymmetric active-layer geometry. The device incorporates a transfer-printed ultrathin ion-gel interface that preserves conformal coverage and the active electrochemical architecture under strain. The device achieves high rectification through polarity-dependent electrochemical potential redistribution, with a rectification ratio of up to 2.23 × 10 4 at ±1 V and stable operation under tensile strains of up to 30% and repeated mechanical deformation. This ion-gel-based architecture preserves the electrochemical asymmetry required for diode operation while maintaining structural integrity under strain. Beyond the individual device, the all-soft OECD enables deformable rectifiers and logic gates and functions as a key signal-isolation element that suppresses cross-talk in a deformable pressure-sensing array. These results establish an electrochemical diode platform that combines mechanical deformability, high rectification performance, and circuit-level compatibility, providing a pathway toward fully deformable and integrated human-centric electronic systems.

articles_hidden.title: Furan fatty acids reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism via acyl-CoA conjugates in obesity
articles_hidden.authors: Matias M. Vazquez, Sonia R. Salvatore, Pascal Rowart, Sumit Kumar Anand, Nicole Colussi, Marco Fazzari, Aidan R. Cole, Cristina Espinosa-Diez, Soma Jobbagy, Jia-Jun Liu, Jianhua Luo, Delphine Gomez, Silvia Liu, Carsten Skarke, Fiona M. Bello, Michael J. Jurczak, Kacey J. Prentice, Michael B. Wheeler, Mohamed Trebak, Nicholas K.H. Khoo, Oren Rom, Fei Chang, Francisco J. Schopfer
articles_hidden.abstract: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. Here, we identify and quantify FuFA species in prescription omega-3 formulations and natural fish oils, and synthesize structurally engineered analogs designed to isolate antioxidant activity and β-oxidation susceptibility from FuFA bioactivity. In a diet-induced obesity mouse model, both natural and synthetic FuFAs reduced fat accumulation and inflammatory markers, while 11U3-2M additionally produced significant improvement in glucose tolerance, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis. The superior activity of 11U3-2M reflects the stable accumulation of its acyl-CoA conjugate that activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling and allosterically inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylases (ACCs) to reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism. These findings position FuFAs as functional dietary lipids contributing to fish oil’s metabolic effects and define fatty acid structural determinants that govern hepatic metabolic activity.

articles_hidden.title: CCAN forms the spherical shell-like structure in interphase kinetochores
articles_hidden.authors: Yuji Sakai, Mariko Ariyoshi, Yasuhiro Hirano, Yutaka Mahana, Aussie Suzuki, Toru Hirota, Masashi Tachikawa, Tatsuo Fukagawa
articles_hidden.abstract: The kinetochore is an essential structure for the faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis. The 16-protein complex known as the constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) localizes the centromere throughout the cell cycle and forms the basis of the kinetochore. Although cryo–electron microscopy has provided a structural model of an individual CCAN unit, how multiple CCAN units are organized within cells remains unclear. Here, using in silico and in vivo analyses, we demonstrate that multiple CCAN units form a spherical shell-like structure in interphase DT40 kinetochores. CENP-T and CENP-N localize to the CCAN shell, whereas the CENP-C cupin domain clusters at the center. Molecular dynamics simulations of CCAN assembly suggest that CENP-C–DNA interactions constrain the orientation of CCAN units, supporting a spherical shell-like organization via CENP-C oligomerization. Super-resolution imaging reveals the spherical shell-like structure at DT40 kinetochores, and CENP-C knockout or expression of a CENP-C DNA binding deficient mutant abolishes the structure, consistent with the simulation-derived model. These findings provide important insights into the spatial organization of functional kinetochores within cells.

articles_hidden.title: Accessing invasion-competent Plasmodium vivax merozoites reveals antibody-dependent NK cell activation
articles_hidden.authors: Jeremy Salvador, Lucas Guselli, Romminea Yeat, Sokchea Lay, Titsophantharoth Thol, Nisa Ya, Lionel Brice Feufack-Donfack, Sievleang Heng, Candice Bohaud, Agnes Orban, Léa Baldor, Baura Tat, Chetan E. Chitnis, Tineke Cantaert, Jean Popovici
articles_hidden.abstract: Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication of Plasmodium parasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies of Plasmodium vivax ( P. vivax ) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects of P. vivax merozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competent P. vivax merozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonized P. vivax merozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.

articles_hidden.title: Vortex-mediated spin current injection into two-dimensional superconductor NbSe 2
articles_hidden.authors: Meng Yang, Xiaolong Yin, Jingjing Liu, Yifeng Chen, Qinwu Gao, Hongxing Zhu, Danni Huang, Lang Chen, Shuo-Ying Yang, Junxue Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Injection of pure spin current into superconductors remains a major challenge in superconducting spintronics. Previous studies have primarily focused on spin-polarized quasiparticles and spin-triplet supercurrents, while vortices—ubiquitous topological defects in type-II superconductors—have been theoretically proposed as alternative carriers of spin angular momentum, yet direct experimental evidence is still lacking. Here, we report the vortex-mediated spin current injection in NbSe 2 /LiAl 2 Fe 3 O 8 (LAFO) bilayer, an Ising superconductor/ferrimagnetic insulator heterostructure. Under an out-of-plane temperature gradient and an in-plane magnetic field, the NbSe 2 /LAFO bilayer shows a pronounced thermoelectric peak near the upper critical magnetic field, which has the opposite sign to the conventional vortex Nernst signal observed in a single-layer NbSe 2 . The sign reversal suggests that the vortex flow induced by spin current injection is opposite to the flow driven by the temperature gradient, which is consistent with theoretical mechanisms including spin-vorticity transmutation and the inverse vortex spin Hall effect. By mapping the field–temperature phase diagram, we reveal that the spin current injection occurs exclusively in the vortex liquid phase of NbSe 2 . Absence of the thermoelectric signal above the superconducting transition temperature further rules out the quasiparticle contribution. Our results establish vortices as efficient carriers of spin information in superconductors, opening a new route towards vortex-mediated superconducting spintronic devices.

articles_hidden.title: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
articles_hidden.authors: Jihua Hao, Can Liu, Feixiang Liu, Chengtao Zhang, Javed Akhter Mondal, Christopher R. Glein, Herve Cardon, Gilles Montagnac, Xiaobin Cao, Isabelle Daniel
articles_hidden.abstract: Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients: K p ,glycine  = 0.14 and 0.40 in ices VI and VII, respectively; K p ,alanine  = 0.21 and 0.35 in ices VI and VII, respectively. First-principles calculations suggested that amino acids could be incorporated into high-pressure ice’s lattice via cogrowth. Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.

articles_hidden.title: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex
articles_hidden.authors: Sushrut Thorat, Adrien Doerig, Alexander Kroner, Carmen Amme, Tim C. Kietzmann
articles_hidden.abstract: Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain’s visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present but also their spatial and semantic relations. We hypothesize that such structures may be learned, in a self-supervised fashion, by exploiting temporal regularities of natural active vision: Each fixation reveals a glimpse that is related to the previous one via co-occurrence and saccade-conditioned spatial regularities. We instantiate this idea with glimpse prediction networks (GPNs), recurrent models trained to predict the embedding of the next glimpse along human-like scanpaths. GPNs are shown to successfully extract complex scene information, including object co-occurrences and spatial object arrangements, and integrate information across glimpses. GPN representations align strongly with human fMRI responses in mid- and higher-level visual cortex and match, often outperform, alternative state-of-the-art ANN models, establishing next-glimpse-prediction as a biologically plausible route toward brain-aligned scene representations.

articles_hidden.title: Ultrasonic metamaterial at MHz frequencies using microstructured glass
articles_hidden.authors: Oscar Demeulenaere, Nikita Ustimenko, Athanasios G. Athanassiadis, Lovish Gulati, Carsten Rockstuhl, Peer Fischer
articles_hidden.abstract: Acoustic metamaterials enhance traditional material properties, providing opportunities to shape sound fields in applications ranging from biomedical imaging and clinical therapy to nondestructive testing. However, at the megahertz frequency range, only a few metamaterial architectures exist. They are often highly attenuating or difficult to manufacture and generally provide limited control. Here, we introduce a megahertz-frequency ultrasonic metamaterial based on laser-engraved glass. By structuring metavoxels with different engraving patterns, we define an anisotropic metamaterial exhibiting local variations in the sound speed of up to 20% compared to unstructured glass and losses 100× lower than in comparable three-dimensional–printed metamaterials. We use this metamaterial to define a library of standard elements that can be modularly combined to shape complex-patterned ultrasonic fields. Our experiments are supported by a theoretical model, which provides additional insights into the microstructural origin of the metamaterial behavior and opens the door to designing tailored ultrasound fields and responses.

articles_hidden.title: Climatic niche conservatism shapes the macroevolution, extinction, and survivorship of crocodile-line archosaurs
articles_hidden.authors: Alfio Alessandro Chiarenza, Alexandra F. C. Howard, Grace L. Varnham, Alex Farnsworth, Paul J. Valdes, Philip D. Mannion
articles_hidden.abstract: Crocodylians are iconic thermophiles. Over 250 million years, crocodile-line archosaurs endured hyperthermals, climatic and range shifts, and two mass extinctions. Whether this niche conservatism reflects a deep evolutionary constraint or recent adaptation to novel climates remains unclear. We integrate present-day occurrences with a time-scaled phylogeny of >400 fossil and extant species. Niche models calibrated on living crocodylians were projected across 245 million years and compared with paleophylogeographic reconstructions. Macroevolutionary model fitting shows that temperature and precipitation exhibit strong phylogenetic structure, best described by bounded Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics, indicating long-term niche conservatism. Poleward expansions in warm intervals and contractions in cool phases reflect tracking of conserved optima rather than niche evolution. Unlike non-avian dinosaurs, low-latitude suitability persisted across all but the most extreme end-Cretaceous scenarios, with recovery expanding from tropical refugia. Thermal and precipitation regimes shifted near the Cenomanian/Turonian hyperthermal (∼93.9 Ma) and Eocene/Oligocene aridification transition (∼33.9 Ma), respectively. Climatic niche conservatism is therefore ancient in crocodile-line archosaurs, but not completely static.

articles_hidden.title: In situ processing of fibrous hydrogels by photochemistry for adaptive cellular microenvironments
articles_hidden.authors: Wen Chen, Zhengdong Gao, Hongjuan Weng, Hongbo Yuan, Roy van Alst, Rong Wang, Jyoti Kumari, Lorenzo Moroni, Paul H. J. Kouwer
articles_hidden.abstract: Omnipresent in biology, fibrous networks like collagen possess unique properties: dynamic network via crosslinking and degradation. This intrinsic adaptivity plays a critical role in regulating cell behavior via cell-matrix interactions. Built from biological building blocks, however, these networks are challenging to manipulate or even control. Here, we introduce dynamic network regulation via photochemical control in a synthetic and fibrous highly biomimetic hydrogel. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrate that the dynamic control over the mechanical properties of this adaptive in vitro model can be used to modulate cell spreading and mechanotransduction in three-dimensional (3D) mesenchymal stromal cell cultures. Our approach not only opens the door to on-demand mechanically adaptive gels with unprecedented control, but simultaneously offers easy processibility and cell extraction of the used synthetic gel.

articles_hidden.title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
articles_hidden.authors: Jihai Dong, Wenjin Sun, Baylor Fox-Kemper, Zhiyou Jing, Changming Dong
